curated-eater-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Eater looks dark and aggressive, with wide gaps between letters. Noto Sans Lepcha gives a sturdy, cast-iron lowercase and curves kept open, which could sit nicely on a creepy carnival poster.
curated-eater-gf-noto-sans-meetei-mayek: Eater's short ascenders and mellow thick-thin shifts give it a dark, aggressive look. Noto Sans Meetei Mayek reads modern and plain over pages, its rounds gapped like a cracked bangle, nothing like gothic cathedral lettering.
curated-fascinate-gf-trocchi: Trocchi has a dignified, wide-open c and gently thinning bowls. Fascinate does the dramatic part, heavy pillars joined by fine wires, while Trocchi handles the steady, small shifts in stroke thickness.
curated-fascinate-inline-lora: Fascinate Inline pulls hard between fat strokes and thread-thin ones, loosely tracked in a vintage, precise way. Lora does the reading, with sturdy hairlines and a welcoming c.
curated-flavors-gf-noto-sans-meroitic: Flavors is a stubby, whimsical display face, tall enough to crown a cake topper, with diagonals as hefty as its stems. Noto Sans Meroitic keeps things approachable, its see-through c openings and capital-sized lowercase filling the line.
curated-freckle-face-gf-vesper-libre: Strip-cut and chunky: Freckle Face has crossbars fat as the stems they connect. Vesper Libre brings a refined, bookish plainness underneath, though it isn't built for long paragraphs of text.
curated-fredoka-gf-annapurna-sil: Annapurna SIL is editorial and refined, with tightly packed letters. Fredoka's rounded, friendly line stays one width throughout, while the body is better bumped up a size, since it prefers brief copy.
curated-fredoka-gf-besley: One unbroken pen width runs through every Fredoka letter. Besley, a dignified serif with robust downstrokes and slender turns, deserves a generous size (handy for a handwriting practice sheet).
curated-fredoka-gf-cardo: Round, friendly, drawn with one constant nib: that's Fredoka. Cardo, literary and dignified, thins its arch shoulders slowly, so give it a touch more size (say, on a kids cooking class flyer).
curated-fredoka-gf-im-fell-dw-pica: Fredoka's letterforms look like bent tubing, one smooth line with an open e, friendly and approachable. IM Fell DW Pica jostles along, literary and refined, happiest with brief copy.
curated-fredoka-gf-im-fell-dw-pica-sc: Friendly Fredoka keeps a single line width with an open e (say, for a cute bakery's identity). But IM Fell DW Pica SC is the bookish one, with moderate stroke modulation, neither wispy nor heavy.
curated-fredoka-gf-im-fell-english-sc: Neon-tube roundness from Fredoka, maybe on a preschool welcome sign. IM Fell English SC, editorial and bookish, reads with soft accents of heavier strokes, a rhythm that keeps moving.
curated-fredoka-gf-im-fell-french-canon-: Friendly and rounded, Fredoka cuts every stroke like ribbon of constant width, never thinning anywhere along a curve. IM Fell French Canon SC: dark pillars, faint wires, best for two lines.
curated-fredoka-gf-libertinus-serif: Libertinus Serif is refined and authoritative, with a slight swell on its bowls. Libertinus Serif leaves the big, short work to Fredoka's monoline strokes, say, a kids camp logo.
curated-fredoka-gf-martel: Fredoka's unvarying line feels friendly, say, on a preschool welcome sign. Martel's classic serif letters, moderate in contrast with horseshoe-open apertures, give the heading's cheer a steady editorial footing.
curated-fredoka-gf-nanum-myeongjo: Friendly and uniform in line: that is Fredoka at its simplest. Nanum Myeongjo, a text serif with quiet modulation and curve tips that never touch, makes the real contrast.
curated-fredoka-gf-tiro-bangla: Fredoka is friendly and approachable, with letters drawn at a single constant line width and an open e. Tiro Bangla's bold stems feel traditional, not made for long paragraphs.
curated-fredoka-gf-volkhov: Friendly Fredoka holds each stroke at one thickness, like drawn cable. Volkhov, a text serif, brings the gentle thick-thin shift of soft pencil beneath it, so the page feels both approachable and traditional.
curated-fs-aktura-fs-rowan: Rowan opens every curve generously, with thin strokes half the weight of thick. Aktura's tall stems and almost knotted s hold the drama, while the text serif Rowan lets the page unwind in friendly, brief visits.
curated-fs-aktura-gf-almendra-sc: Dignified Almendra SC keeps its mouths open on every curve. Aktura's tall closed letters carry the command, so give Almendra SC a touch more size and it stays comfortable for brief reading.
curated-fs-aktura-gf-nuosu-sil: Nuosu SIL, the plain sans here, keeps lowercase modest as chalk dots. Nuosu SIL's open shapes sit against Aktura's dramatic, near-knotted s and tall stems, comfortable for brief reading.
curated-fs-aktura-gf-overpass-mono: Overpass Mono reads loose and structured, every letter on a fixed width. Next to Aktura's dramatic, tightly closed letters, the monospace body feels open and orderly, comfortable for brief stretches.
curated-fs-aktura-gf-red-hat-mono: Red Hat Mono moves at a measured cadence, with long beats between letters. The sharpest thing here is the foil: Aktura's commanding stems against Red Hat Mono's ballpoint-fine line, which tires over lengthy paragraphs.
curated-fs-aktura-gf-yuji-boku: Aktura stands tall and knotted-shut in its s, dramatic and commanding, against Yuji Boku's wide-open c like a bracelet pulled apart. Yuji Boku's cable-like strokes become wearing page after page.
curated-fs-array-bitter: Futuristic and precise, Array keeps its curves open-ended and its lowercase eyes large. Bitter, a grounded slab-serif with a see-through s, stays dependable across a page, though it was made for brief sittings.
curated-fs-array-gf-league-gothic: Sharp, tall and tightly packed, League Gothic runs narrow beneath Array's open curves and large lowercase eyes. Array is best at looking futuristic up top; League Gothic is best at squeezing words in.
curated-fs-array-gf-noto-sans-display: Noto Sans Display is an approachable sans with a tall middle zone, backing Array's futuristic headings (a racing game ui, say). Read at length, it stays approachable but is really made for brief stretches.
curated-fs-bevellier-roboto-slab: Roboto Slab carries a dense middle zone and open throats in a, c, e and s, while Bevellier above it looks stencil-cut and close-fitted. Roboto Slab keeps things structured, and Bevellier adds a graceful, flat-cut flourish beside it.
curated-fs-bonny-gf-commissioner: Bonny has a subtle weight shift, like lines etched in glass. Commissioner holds one thickness through every curve, so the smooth sans body gives those fine shifts room to be noticed.
curated-fs-bonny-gf-dotgothic16: Gently pressed and literary, Bonny thins its diagonals just below its verticals. DotGothic16 keeps a tube-like single line weight through every bend, sturdy enough even for a jewelry card.
curated-fs-bonny-gf-elms-sans: Bonny has a literary, understated stroke variation, like lines lightly etched. Elms Sans, a sans-serif, runs a plain ballpoint line with a see-through s, so paragraphs would flow smoothly, say on a leatherwork stamp.
curated-fs-bonny-gf-jost: Jost reads with broad gaps at the terminals and pencil-like lines that never thicken or thin. And Bonny's soft shifts in thickness make it the warmer partner, which is the real draw, even for a soap and bath products label.
curated-fs-bonny-gf-mohave: Bonny looks literary, tightly set and shaded somewhere between monoline and sharp contrast. Mohave, a sans with crossbar and stem in matching strength, gives that soft shading something steady to sit against.
curated-fs-bonny-gf-monda: Bonny has the moderate thinning of letters stamped in soft metal, which gives headings a refined, literary tone. Monda keeps small counters unclogged, say for a workshop class sign up.
curated-fs-bonny-gf-noto-sans-cypriot: Refined and literary, Bonny keeps its lines tightly set. Where Bonny draws quiet distinction between upstroke and downstroke, Noto Sans Cypriot simply opens its e and keeps text easy going.
curated-fs-bonny-gf-noto-sans-nko-unjoin: Noto Sans NKo Unjoined reads friendly, with wide openings on small letters. Across a full column it stays easygoing and unhurried, while Bonny's low-key thick-thin shading adds a literary note above.
curated-fs-bonny-gf-noto-sans-shavian: Noto Sans Shavian brings contemporary, rope-loose curves that never knot. Under Bonny's quietly modulated, literary headings, those loose curves feel clean and modern, a sans-serif that lets the serif do the talking.
curated-fs-bonny-gf-pt-sans: Approachable PT Sans draws its c as an open arc. Beneath Bonny's slight tug of heavier verticals against lighter horizontals, it stays friendly and steady, good for a soap and bath products line.
curated-fs-bonny-gf-sawarabi-gothic: Sawarabi Gothic reads contemporary, with open jaws on every curve. Bonny is the one for literary polish, its thin strokes close to its thick, while Sawarabi Gothic handles plain, steady reading.
curated-fs-bonny-gf-signika-negative: Bonny sets literary tone with thin strokes only slightly lighter than its thick ones and tightly packed lines. Beneath it, Signika Negative offers modern, no-fuss plain sans text for the body.
curated-fs-bonny-gf-zalando-sans: Refined and literary, Bonny swells and tapers gently along its curves. Zalando Sans sits beneath as an approachable sans with open-ended curves, so the serif heading gets room to talk.
curated-fs-boxing-gf-sura: Energetic and bold, Boxing draws bowls and stems at one weight with generous sidebearings. Sura, a traditional serif with slightly thinner hairlines, is the one to size up a notch for a handful of authoritative lines.
curated-fs-britney-gf-ancizar-sans: Ancizar Sans packs its glyphs in tight, like keys on a typewriter bank, with a modern, neutral manner. Over a longer stretch it reads dense and orderly, a firm counterweight to Britney's relaxed script.
curated-fs-britney-gf-cabin-condensed: Britney's calligraphic hand feels relaxed and expressive, best kept to a few words (a cute bakery, say). And Cabin Condensed, plain sans with ribbon-like constant strokes, carries the fuller text.
curated-fs-britney-gf-carme: Relaxed and expressive, Britney leans into a tight calligraphic hand. Carme follows in a modern line with open counters, so give it a bit more size than usual.
curated-fs-britney-gf-commissioner: Relaxed and expressive, Britney writes with a narrow, calligraphic hand. Commissioner, a smooth sans with unclogged curves, carries the reading, and it holds up nicely over a few lines of text.
curated-fs-britney-gf-economica: Economica is clamped down tight, tubelike lines nearly touching, which could sit nicely beside a youtube channel logo. Britney's script loosens everything up, and Economica can take a slightly larger size so its narrow letters stay readable.
curated-fs-britney-gf-m-plus-code-latin: M PLUS Code Latin reads friendly and clean, like neon tubing. Britney's relaxed calligraphic script, say, for a wedding invitation, sits above it, and the wide-mouthed letters below keep the whole page approachable.
curated-fs-britney-gf-monda: Monda keeps its small counters open and friendly. Britney's script heading has pipe-like strokes against Monda's low, plain build, and the pair is good for a few lines of text.
curated-fs-britney-gf-niramit: Niramit reads professional and clean, its curves gaping wide open. Britney does best with its flowing script lines, no modulation in the stroke, while Niramit is the one built to carry actual sentences.
curated-fs-britney-gf-rufina: Rufina feels bookish, its fat vertical stems joined by hairline connectors, say, for an anthology cover. Britney is the one for flowing script with a fixed-pressure stroke, while Rufina does the sturdy, traditional text work.
curated-fs-britney-gf-source-sans-3: Source Sans 3 lets its lower a bowl open up and breathe. Britney's heading strokes look like bent neon glass, while the body stays low-key, and it does better when text is brief.
curated-fs-britney-gf-tiro-devanagari-ma: Relaxed and expressive, Britney writes in a calligraphic hand with narrow room around every letter. Big and short is where it works, while Tiro Devanagari Marathi, an editorial serif, glitters with dark and light strokes for brief copy.
curated-fs-britney-gf-urbanist: Loose, flowing script on top, then a single-width pen trail below. Britney does its best work in a few lines of narrow, calligraphic hand, while Urbanist carries the steadier reading underneath.
curated-fs-chubbo-fs-literata: Chubbo draws casual, inviting letters with a smooth marker-tip bend. Literata, a bookish serif with sturdy thin lines and modest thickening, supplies the real hook: rope-like friendliness meeting sophisticated restraint.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-agdasima: Chubbo rolls out casual marker-tip letters with smooth, unbroken curves. Agdasima, a sans-serif, is the tighter counterpart: packed, fineliner-thin and modern, where Chubbo is loose, friendly and generous.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-alan-sans: Chubbo lays down strokes as steady as a pulled string, friendly enough for a kids bedtime story. Alan Sans keeps its curve tails back, so the heading gets the spotlight.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-average-sans: Average Sans moves at a cramped pace that rushes the eye. Chubbo's uniform, marker-like strokes keep the heading casual and inviting, while the body's tight pace is best left to brief text.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-barlow-semi-condens: Casual, marker-tip Chubbo could front a rainbow unicorn party. Barlow Semi Condensed, with its hugged-together lines, heavy bowls and wide-mouthed rounds, benefits from a slightly larger body text size.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-biz-udmincho: Inviting, marker-drawn Chubbo could headline, say, a dinosaur book cover. Over longer stretches, BIZ UDMincho reads in a traditional, bookish way, its shallow terminal curls and wide gaps keeping lines open.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-cairo-play: Chubbo's flat, marker-tip strokes (think a dinosaur book cover) feel friendly. The heading does casual personality best, while Cairo Play, a sans, does its best work in clear, open round letters at small sizes.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-danfo: Danfo, authoritative and generously spaced, sits in the body (a sleepover invitation, maybe). Chubbo's marker-tip curves loosen things up top, while the serif's narrow e channels and brief-burst reading keep the text focused.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-denk-one: Soft marker curves, cute as a thank you note. Chubbo does open, full-bodied letters best, while Denk One, a sans, does tighter openings and moderate contrast well, suited to brief bursts.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-enriqueta: Every stem and arc in Chubbo moves in lockstep, drawn as if with a marker tip. Enriqueta adds literary, dignified curves that stop short of closing, giving the marker-drawn heading a more formal partner.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-gantari: Chubbo glides around every bend like a marker tip. It earns its keep big and short, as on a fairy tale book cover, with Gantari's wire-bent sans-serif lines following quietly.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-hanken-grotesk: Hanken Grotesk keeps a wire-bent, clean look while Chubbo's marker-tip letters could headline a kids camp logo. Long paragraphs of it glide along, with wide channels leading into each counter.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-imprima: Imprima has a smooth, tube-like look, its terminals flaring outward. Page after page it reads friendly and entirely unfussy, a quiet partner for Chubbo's casual, marker-drawn headings up top.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-inria-sans: Inria Sans runs like bent copper pipe, with see-through c openings. Chubbo does best at loud, smooth marker-tip swagger, while the sans-serif does best at carrying sentences without fuss.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-jura: Chubbo curves smoothly, every letter drawn as if with a marker tip. Its job is inviting warmth; Jura's is constant, wire-bent strokes with s curves opening wide at both ends.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-kodchasan: Chubbo is casual and inviting, drawn as if with a marker tip. Beside it, Kodchasan's hanging-open terminals and unthinned strokes feel clean and friendly, say, on an animal alphabet poster.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-m-plus-1: M PLUS 1 has a flat fineliner line and big open eyes. Under Chubbo's smooth, marker-tip headings it settles in as the sans-serif text, crisp where the headings are rounded.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-m-plus-2: M PLUS 2 reads friendly: a gaping c, one fixed nib width. Chubbo handles the loose, inviting work up front; the sans-serif handles keeping text tidy and approachable behind it.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-national-park: Smooth marker curves lead, then a pen that never shifts pressure. Chubbo supplies the casual welcome, while National Park's rounded, open-sided sans letters are happy to be sized up a touch.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-news-cycle: Chubbo's strokes carry no shading at all, just marker-smooth curves. The standout quality is how News Cycle's tight, dense lowercase, with an open-curved g, sets off the heading's shading-free ease.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-niramit: Chubbo draws its letters as if with a marker tip, smooth and unbroken around every bend. Niramit follows with a cleaner, more professional voice, its curves gaping open so the heading's casual warmth has something tidy to lean on.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-noto-sans-new-tai-l: Cupped, rounded letters read softly and openly, never clenched. Noto Sans New Tai Lue stays low-key beneath Chubbo's marker-tip headings (say, on a dinosaur book cover), and a page of it reads steadily.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-palanquin: Round-tipped and friendly: Chubbo's blunt marker strokes lead up top, with Palanquin's professional, contemporary, wide-mouthed curves following along below. Chubbo really earns its keep when it's big and short.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-pt-sans-narrow: Chubbo is casual and inviting, with a smooth marker-tip line. PT Sans Narrow, tightly kerned and approachable, suits quick lines like a hen do or stag banner, not pages of paragraphs.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-rationale: Rationale bunches its letters with tiny gaps, a contemporary body under Chubbo's marker-tip heading (a bubble tea launch, say). Dense reading wears thin quickly, so keep it to tiny bites.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-red-hat-text: Chubbo arrives in smooth, marker-drawn curves, casual and inviting. Red Hat Text, say, for a handwriting practice sheet, a plain sans with technical-pen lines and unclamped curves, gives that friendliness a modern, approachable footing.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-sarabun: Chubbo's marker-tip letters take every bend smoothly, with diagonals as stout as its uprights, casual and inviting. Sarabun's wide channel into each bowl rewards a heading sized generously.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-shippori-antique-b1: Loose, marker-pen swagger up top, then daylight through every curve below. Shrink Chubbo down and its chunky charm gets lost, while Shippori Antique B1 blown up large loses its sans restraint.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-signika: Signika reads modern and plain, with no fuss in its build. Chubbo's monoline marker stroke brings the casual warmth, while the sans below it keeps the page grounded and current.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-spinnaker: Spinnaker keeps its counters connected to the outside space. Chubbo's marker-tip letters supply the friendly, inviting energy, and the two make a modern, easygoing pair (a kids cooking class flyer, maybe).
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-stick: Chubbo draws smooth marker-tip letters that glide around every bend. Stick trails behind in tubelike, constant-weight strokes with wide exits, and Chubbo can take the larger size (an animal alphabet poster, maybe).
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-tajawal: Marker-tip friendliness, with smooth curves that flow freely, makes Chubbo feel right at home on a kids party store sign. Tajawal keeps plain sans letters with broad open hooks out of the way.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-vazirmatn: Vazirmatn brings an s that never tightens, a modern, approachable partner for Chubbo's marker-steady lines (say, a fairy tale book cover). Chubbo is the casual, inviting one; Vazirmatn keeps things approachable.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-voltaire: Chubbo is casual and inviting, with letters traced as if by one marker. Voltaire sits snug and compact beneath it, a sans better for brief lines than for long, unbroken paragraphs.
curated-fs-chubbo-gf-zcool-kuaile: ZCOOL KuaiLe is a wire-like monoline sans-serif that feels approachable, and it follows Chubbo's marker-tip curves without any fuss. What holds them together is that shared one-line, hand-drawn feel.
curated-fs-comico-fs-paquito: Whimsical and commanding, Comico spreads its poured-lead lowercase wide. Comico is best at one loud line, while Paquito, confident and approachable, is better at brief text than long paragraphs.
curated-fs-comico-gf-bree-serif: Bree Serif brings literary, refined lowercase with outsized proportions, a text companion that is better for brief lines than long paragraphs. Comico does the shouting; Bree Serif does the talking.
curated-fs-comico-gf-chivo-mono: Poured-lead lowercase, spread wide, gives Comico a whimsical, commanding swagger up top. Chivo Mono, a monospace with scissor-blade terminals, sits next to it like a technical drawing beside a cartoon, made for quick reads.
curated-fs-comico-gf-montserrat-alternat: Whimsical and spread wide, Comico plants heavy lowercase like poured lead. Where Comico commands attention, Montserrat Alternates does the talking in plain sans, with open round letters and lowercase that crowds the capital line.
curated-fs-excon-gf-athiti: Excon packs its towering lowercase tight, like chalk marks on a full slate. Athiti shares that build, with see-through s shapes and a high mean line, so shrinking Excon or enlarging Athiti makes them nearly indistinguishable.
curated-fs-excon-gf-biryani: Chalk-crowded and friendly, Excon and Biryani look cut from the same cloth. Both are plain sans with open, unclogged shapes and no stroke variation, handy for a painting contractor, say.
curated-fs-excon-gf-candal: Excon packs its letters close and keeps its terminals open. Candal spreads out below it, with wide round counters and curves that close up, so the page moves from tight to loose.
curated-fs-excon-gf-carlito: Carlito keeps its round letters open and its spacing tight, with capitals that look small beside the lowercase. Excon draws a skeleton outline at one fixed thickness, while Carlito's strokes vary a little more, which gives each its own job.
curated-fs-excon-gf-huninn: Huninn reads modern and brisk, its lowercase rising close to cap height, handy for a moving company, say. Excon, crowded and chalky, sits snugly with it, both sans-serif.
curated-fs-excon-gf-michroma: Michroma spreads wide beneath the spaghetti-like strokes of Excon, fine for a trucking company, say. Michroma lets plain sans letters, each given a wide berth, keep text moving smoothly down a full page.
curated-fs-excon-gf-noto-sans-carian: Noto Sans Carian reads with terminals that stay apart like open scissor blades, ideal for a glass and window shop, say. Excon holds a line of near-zero contrast and crowds its letters, while Noto Sans Carian simply opens them up.
curated-fs-excon-gf-noto-sans-elymaic: Excon crowds its letters tight, while Noto Sans Elymaic keeps its ascenders barely above the x-height (think glass and window). Open shapes are the common thread, clean and modern in both.
curated-fs-excon-gf-noto-sans-grantha: Excon crowds its letters like chalk marks on a full slate, with a steady, marker-like line. Noto Sans Grantha, a plain sans, keeps its bowls tall and open, so reading never snags.
curated-fs-excon-gf-noto-sans-jp: Chalk-tight and friendly, Excon leads (on an electrician business card, say). Noto Sans JP lifts the pair with its very tall x-height and curves that sweep open instead of curling shut.
curated-fs-excon-gf-noto-sans-nag-mundar: Chalk-tight and friendly up top, Excon would look at home on construction equipment decals, with its open terminals. Noto Sans Nag Mundari backs it with plain sans, half-unwrapped curves.
curated-fs-excon-gf-noto-sans-siddham: Approachable Excon crowds its letters like chalk marks on a full slate, while Noto Sans Siddham spreads out (a painting contractor, say). Its large middle band keeps paragraphs easy to follow.
curated-fs-excon-gf-noto-sans-syloti-nag: Noto Sans Syloti Nagri reads clean, with short ascenders and a tall x-height, say for a moving company. But Excon is the one that grabs attention, with crowded letters, while the body just keeps things clear.
curated-fs-excon-gf-noto-sans-thaana: Approachable from the start, Excon packs its letters in tight. Noto Sans Thaana brings wide channels into each counter and big open lowercase forms, giving the dense heading room to breathe beside it.
curated-fs-excon-gf-noto-sans-vithkuqi: Excon packs towering, chalk-crowded letters at a single line weight, while Noto Sans Vithkuqi stays open (think fleet vehicle livery). Its open throats keep text moving smoothly, paragraph after paragraph.
curated-fs-excon-gf-nova-mono: Nova Mono draws like a technical pen, precise, with a generous c. Excon's crowded, towering lowercase takes the top, and the monospace lines beneath read like careful annotations.
curated-fs-excon-gf-readex-pro: Excon crowds its letters like chalk marks, and Readex Pro meets it with broad terminal gaps and a tiny step from lowercase to caps. Mostly, they share one build, and that sameness holds it together.
curated-fs-excon-gf-secular-one: Approachable and chalk-tight, Excon could headline a glass and window sign. Secular One matches it with a dominant midsection and no stroke variation, so both look like plain sans cut from one block.
curated-fs-excon-gf-sintony: Tight chalk-mark letters up top, with towering lowercase. Excon does its best work at full strength with uniform strokes, while Sintony's chunky midzone keeps curves smooth and unclogged.
curated-fs-expose-gf-bayon: Bayon hugs its letter edges, with round o's walled at a constant thickness, beneath Expose and its compressed cadence. Built for brief reads, it stays friendly throughout.
curated-fs-gambarino-fs-bespoke-sans: Bespoke Sans keeps generous space between curve ends and the stem, sharp and refined (think gift shop tissue paper). Gambarino does heavy-stemmed drama best, the body does quiet order.
curated-fs-kalam-gf-afacad: Kalam feels cozy and hand-drawn, its lines bundled tight, and it earns its keep big and short. Afacad, a plain sans bent like glass tubing, suits quick reads, as on a pizza shop menu.
curated-fs-kalam-gf-alatsi: Cozy, hand-drawn Kalam gives the heading its warmth, and the lines look tightly bundled. Alatsi is the plainer, approachable body, comfortable in small doses, so give it a bit more size than you might expect.
curated-fs-kalam-gf-bbh-hegarty: Hand-drawn and cozy, Kalam bundles its lines tightly, the sort of look a fitness wordmark could borrow. BBH Hegarty is a modern, sparse foil, snug enough for brief doses.
curated-fs-kalam-gf-bhutuka-expanded-one: Cozy handwriting up top, then a literary text serif below. Kalam bundles its lines with a hand-drawn feel, while BhuTuka Expanded One runs curvy and unclamped, its stroke uniform throughout.
curated-fs-kalam-gf-cabin-condensed: Cabin Condensed reads snug, its letters nearly touching in ribbon-like strokes. Kalam adds a cozy, hand-drawn bundle of lines on top, and the pair is comfortable when taken in modest sips.
curated-fs-kalam-gf-gabriela: Gabriela reads classic and authoritative, though it is not meant for long paragraphs. Kalam brings the hand-drawn warmth up top, and the body's gently tapering strokes supply some quiet authority beneath it.
curated-fs-kalam-gf-gelasio: Gelasio brings a faint swell to every curve, like pulled taffy. Beside Kalam's cozy hand-drawn lines it adds a bookish, traditional warmth, strongest on short wording like a letterpress invitation.
curated-fs-kalam-gf-gupter: Kalam is hand-drawn through and through, cozy and tightly bundled, a nice fit for a hair accessories label. But Gupter's gently swelling serif curves add editorial polish, though it isn't built for lengthy paragraphs.
curated-fs-kalam-gf-hubballi: Crammed like nails in a jar, this sans-serif body reads contemporary, though lengthy reading isn't its job (a jewelry card, say). Hubballi pulls its strokes like solder through a nozzle, a crisp foil for Kalam's cozy hand-drawn lines.
curated-fs-kalam-gf-inknut-antiqua: Dignified Inknut Antiqua spaces its letters wide, like ticks on a tape measure. Kalam brings a cozy, hand-drawn heading above it, good for a handful of lines, while the serif body keeps its curves restrained.
curated-fs-kalam-gf-kanit: Tightly bundled, hand-drawn warmth from Kalam leads the way. Kanit is the plain sans underneath, staying out of the way in text that is meant to be skimmed briefly.
curated-fs-kalam-gf-ledger: Ledger brings dignified, bookish shading with a measured stroke contrast, nice on a maker story card. Ledger beside Kalam's cozy hand-drawn lines is a dignified-meets-friendly meeting, better left to brief wording.
curated-fs-kalam-gf-palanquin-dark: Cozy handwriting meets plain sans-serif strokes, with Kalam up top and Palanquin Dark below (a bar mitzvah invitation, say). Kalam charms with hand-drawn warmth; Palanquin Dark stays modern, fine in modest bursts.
curated-fs-kalam-gf-playfair: Kalam has a hand-drawn, tightly bundled look that feels inviting. Playfair, a traditional serif with pale threads between heavy stems, gives text a dignified feel, though it is happiest running just a few lines.
curated-fs-kalam-gf-reddit-mono: Kalam looks hand-drawn, cozy and tightly bundled, like a friendly scribble. Big and short is where it earns its keep, as on a neighborhood association logo, while Reddit Mono suits brief stretches.
curated-fs-kalam-gf-stoke: Kalam's hand-drawn, tightly bundled lines could greet a woodworking shop sign. Where that heading wins on personality, Stoke's quiet, brushed-watercolor shifts in line weight do the reading, though only in brief.
curated-fs-kalam-gf-tiro-devanagari-sans: Cozy handwriting up top, with a refined and authoritative serif below. Kalam's tightly bundled lines sit against the bold stems and wire-thin horizontals of Tiro Devanagari Sanskrit, so skip long paragraphs.
curated-fs-kalam-gf-tiro-kannada: Cozy and hand-drawn, Kalam leads over a refined Tiro Kannada serif, maybe for a yoga logo. Swollen curves against hairline joins: that tension is the draw, in modest portions.
curated-fs-kalam-gf-vollkorn: Kalam brings handwritten warmth to, say, a sticker shop. Vollkorn's steady, faintly modulated line gives that looseness something dignified to lean on, though it's built for brief reading, not endless paragraphs.
curated-fs-kalam-gf-zcool-kuaile: Inviting and cozy, Kalam writes in tightly bundled, hand-drawn lines that feel personal. ZCOOL KuaiLe supplies the wire-like monoline skeleton, an approachable foil that is happiest with brief snippets.
curated-fs-kalam-gf-zen-antique: Zen Antique reads literary, with razor-thin serifs on dense pillars. Kalam does cozy handwriting best (a tech startup wordmark, say), while Zen Antique does steel-nib swell and hairline for quick reading.
curated-fs-khand-gf-abhaya-libre: Abhaya Libre cranks up its stroke contrast; Khand, crisp, has none. Abhaya Libre, with open-faced curves and nib-like fat stems, gives long stretches of text an editorial, dignified pace.
curated-fs-khand-gf-alike-angular: Crisp Khand has no stroke contrast and very close spacing. Alike Angular takes over with a mid-range swing between bold and faint strokes, a traditional voice under the heading.
curated-fs-khand-gf-cardo: Cardo reads literary and dignified, with softly varied strokes. Under Khand's ruler-straight headings, a dense product requirements document would glide along smoothly, since Cardo's counters stay open across paragraphs.
curated-fs-khand-gf-charis-sil: Bookish and dignified, Charis SIL shows a slight but noticeable stroke contrast that never turns dramatic. And Khand, cut at a single depth with tight spacing, keeps the headline crisp while the serif carries a long read without strain.
curated-fs-khand-gf-diphylleia: Diphylleia has a classic, bookish look, with a measured swell from hairline to stem and apertures that stay open even when tiny. Khand's pen never changes pressure, so the long read stays gentle.
curated-fs-khand-gf-gentium-book-plus: Khand sets a crisp, contemporary headline, its stems and arcs moving in lockstep with tight spacing. Gentium Book Plus follows with lighter horizontals and wide letter openings, which keeps a longer stretch of text traditional and easy on the eye.
curated-fs-khand-gf-gupter: Gupter tucks its letters in tightly, with a visible gap at the end of every c. Gupter handles the traditional, editorial text, while Khand's crisp, flat strokes grab attention (on a sticker sheet, say).
curated-fs-khand-gf-ibarra-real-nova: Ibarra Real Nova reads editorial, with fat strokes pulling hard against slender ones, unlike Khand's uniform lines. Ibarra Real Nova keeps longer text inviting, since its bowls stay unclosed.
curated-fs-khand-gf-mate: Mate reads soft and dignified, its round letters cupped and its strokes thinning gently. Khand is the crisp, tube-like one up top, while Mate does the patient work below, say, in a feasibility study.
curated-fs-khand-gf-mate-sc: Crisp Khand tucks its letters close, with no heavy-to-light shifts. Mate SC, a classic serif, brings faint nib-pressure variation to its round letters, so the page moves from uniform strokes to softly pressured ones.
curated-fs-khand-gf-noto-serif-hk: Contemporary Khand reads like signage, plain in every line weight. Khand is best at crisp, tight headlines, while Noto Serif HK offers gentle pen-like modulation in its bowls and generous gaps where curves end.
curated-fs-khand-gf-old-standard-tt: Khand lays down a plain stripe of constant ink. Old Standard TT, a classic serif, is built of heavy pillars and fine wires that nearly vanish, so it's better with brief text than long.
curated-fs-khand-gf-rufina: Bookish Rufina brings fat vertical strokes and filament-thin connectors. Khand, drawn like bent wire, holds steady beside Rufina's high-contrast strokes, and the serif is happiest on a short visit.
curated-fs-khand-gf-sedan: Khand draws round letters like bent wire, tight and stencil-crisp. Sedan, a classic serif, answers below with mellow thick-thin strokes and open terminals, so the headline feels sharp and the text feels bookish.
curated-fs-khand-gf-sura: Sharp and spare, Khand draws a line that never swells or tapers. Sura, a serif, thins its bowls gracefully but not sharply, with slightly thinner hairlines and terminals that never close in.
curated-fs-kohinoor-zerone-gf-frank-ruhl: Kohinoor Zerone draws round letters like bent wire, its o equally heavy on the sides and across the top. Frank Ruhl Libre, a serif, has razor-fine joins; skip long paragraphs.
curated-fs-kohinoor-zerone-gf-kaisei-har: Round letters bent like wire give Kohinoor Zerone a precise, contemporary look. And Kaisei HarunoUmi, built from fat bars and fine threads, handles brief bookish reading while the heading could carry, say, a photographer signature mark.
curated-fs-kola-dm-sans: Kola is best at bold, plain statements up top. DM Sans does the friendly part, with wide-set terminals on its s, and is better with short lines than long paragraphs.
curated-fs-kola-gf-noto-sans-old-south-a: Distinctive Kola keeps its display letters plain and bold. Noto Sans Old South Arabian is the approachable, clean one, with curved strokes that stop before turning inward, and it's best on short text.
curated-fs-new-title-fs-familjen-grotesk: Familjen Grotesk reads lively, its bowls left open on one side. Beneath New Title's bold, chain-linked letters, it carries paragraph after paragraph with a brisk, easy pace, never tiring the eye.
curated-fs-new-title-fs-fira-sans: Fira Sans reads wide and generous, its s curves flaring open at both ends. New Title brings tall, interlocked display letters on top, while the body's uniform tubing-like strokes keep everything beneath it easy to follow.
curated-fs-new-title-fs-pilcrow-rounded:
Pilcrow Rounded packs its letters in tight, with curves left open.

New Title is the bold, chain-linked one with low-slung lowercase, whereas Pilcrow Rounded builds its tall lowercase from rods and big counters, not carved blades.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-abeezee: Tall lowercase locked together like links in a fine chain gives New Title its bold, modern grip. ABeeZee, drawn like neon tubing with a high mean line, feels friendly beside it.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-amiko: Linked-up tall lowercase gives New Title a bold, modern look that stands out immediately. Amiko follows with chunky crayon-height strokes and outward-pointing terminals, so the sans-serif text feels sturdy next to it.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-anaheim: Bold, tight, and modern: New Title links its tall lowercase like a fine chain. Anaheim then lets the eye slide through its dense, rounded sans, with lowercase that fills each line almost like capitals.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-anek-gurmukhi: Anek Gurmukhi opens its small letters with big counters. Beneath New Title's bold, chain-linked display forms, long paragraphs of this sans would feel clear, clean and easy on the eye.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-anek-tamil: Contemporary in feel, New Title pulls its tall lowercase into a bold, chain-like row. Anek Tamil then brings big round bowls and half-unwrapped curves, so a long passage in this sans-serif moves along gently.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-anuphan: Clean, round and open, Anuphan has big lowercase bowls with clear gaps between curves. Under New Title's bold chain-linked display letters, it could suit a cannabis dispensary logo, and a modest body size would do nicely.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-arsenal-sc: New Title's bold, chain-linked letters could front a training deck. Give it large, brief lines, and let Arsenal SC's wide mouths and a faint but real thick-thin shift carry the rest.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-funnel-sans:
Funnel Sans keeps its strokes uniform from stem to curve.

New Title brings a bold, chain-linked punch up top, and the sans below stays tidy, with an e opened like a pried clasp.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-geo: Geo reads clean and tight, fine on a plumber van logo. Against New Title's tall, chained-together bold letters, its single constant stroke gives the whole layout a steady, tidy counterweight.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-gurajada: Tight and tall: New Title locks its letters like chain links. Gurajada's plain sans planks sit close with nearly enclosed round counters, so it works as a counterpoint but isn't meant for long paragraphs.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-holtwood-one-sc: Holtwood One SC stands tall and wide-tracked, its curves nearly closed (a cannabis dispensary logo, say). And line after line it would read loud and weighty, with New Title's locked-together letters adding to the pull.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-lexend-tera: New Title links its letters together like a fine chain. Lexend Tera takes over with a single plotter-pen line, its sans-serif letters spaced like stepping stones against that tight chain.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-major-mono-displ: Major Mono Display glows like neon tubing, precise and technical. Its monospace letters, spaced wide, would march across lines at a slow, deliberate pace, while New Title stays tall and tightly linked.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-mukta-malar: Chunky chain-link headings meet a friendlier, shorter-stemmed text. New Title's tall lowercase makes the loud first move (think company all hands), and Mukta Malar's compressed ascenders keep the sans text approachable.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-noto-sans-displa: Bold from the first glance, New Title locks its letters like chain links. New Title grabs attention; Noto Sans Display keeps every word approachable thanks to a tall middle zone.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-noto-sans-mro: New Title links tall lowercase like a chain, say in a guidelines deck. Noto Sans Mro sits underneath with dense, tall-middled words and wide entrances into each letter, keeping the display lines grounded.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-noto-sans-psalte: New Title links tall lowercase together like a fine chain, bold and modern (think a guidelines deck). Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi stays low and approachable, its e wide-mouthed and its capitals barely rising.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-noto-sans-rejang: Noto Sans Rejang opens its lowercase into wide glass portholes, as an event sponsorship deck might want. And New Title does the loud work, its tall lowercase locked like chain links.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-noto-sans-syriac: New Title is bold and modern, with tall lowercase and letters linked like a fine chain. Noto Sans Syriac Eastern reads approachably, its curves never crowding each other.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-odor-mean-chey: Tall and chained: New Title, say for a yoga logo. New Title does the bold, modern shouting, while Odor Mean Chey brings dignified editorial text with squeezed a, e and s.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-oxygen: Oxygen has lowercase nearly matching its capitals, with curves left open. New Title's tall, chain-linked lowercase gets a clean, contemporary partner in that sans-serif text, which keeps the loud display lines company.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-parkinsans: Crisp, wide-mouthed body text sits under a tall, chained display face. Parkinsans keeps one stroke thickness throughout, so shrinking New Title would lose its chain-link charm while Parkinsans stays sharp.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-ramabhadra: Modern in spirit, New Title links tall lowercase like a fine chain. Give the heading room at display sizes, and let Ramabhadra, with its prominent x-height, carry the clean text beneath.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-rum-raisin: Clean and snug, Rum Raisin has large-eyed lowercase (handy for a real estate logo). And New Title takes the bold lead up top, its tall lowercase linked like chain, with Rum Raisin keeping the text tight.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-savate: Savate keeps its hairlines sturdy and its curves open, with a tall rounded o that nearly matches the capital O. Against it, New Title's tight chain-link lowercase is the real hook.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-sofia-sans-conde: New Title is bold and modern, its tall lowercase linked like a chain. Sofia Sans Condensed follows with one tube-like track width and a big x-height, so longer text (an event sponsorship deck, maybe) feels approachable and unfussy.
curated-fs-new-title-gf-ubuntu-sans: New Title hooks its lowercase together like links in a fine chain, bold and modern. And Ubuntu Sans, tubular like bent copper pipe, has no hairlines anywhere, a sturdy foil for that fine chain.
curated-fs-new-title-manrope: Chain-link headings meet a marker-like body line (a jewelry stamp, say). New Title leads with tall lowercase, then Manrope keeps its pen line at one width, so paragraphs read smoothly and approachably.
curated-fs-new-title-poppins: Poppins reads smooth and rounded, with no heavy-to-light flicker catching the eye. Poppins does its best work in running text, while New Title does its best in big, chain-tight display lines.
curated-fs-new-title-work-sans: Work Sans leaves its c tips well apart, with a high mean line. New Title is best at tall, tightly linked display lettering; Work Sans is best at wire-like, tubular lines with room to breathe.
curated-fs-oswald-fs-bespoke-sans: Oswald stands tall and tightly packed, confident from the first line. Bespoke Sans takes over below, sharp and refined, with generous gaps where its curves leave the stem and loosen each line.
curated-fs-oswald-gf-alef: Confident, tightly knit Oswald takes the lead up top. Oswald is best at strong, compact display rows, while sans-serif Alef is best at clean, modern text with open-ended curves throughout.
curated-fs-oswald-gf-almarai: Tight and confident, Oswald leads while Almarai draws one unswelling line, fine for an architecture portfolio. The standout is Almarai's openness: letters that never seem to pinch shut.
curated-fs-oswald-gf-amarna: Amarna reads clean, its stroke running contrast-free from stem to terminal. Beneath Oswald's tightly knit, confident rows, Amarna's unclogged counters let the text breathe, a clear step down in intensity.
curated-fs-oswald-gf-ancizar-serif: Oswald, tight and confident, could front a cannabis dispensary logo. Oswald is best at compact, strong display rows; Ancizar Serif is best at bookish, editorial text with a gaping c and gently engraved contrast.
curated-fs-oswald-gf-andada-pro: Andada Pro feels traditional and bookish, say, in a nonprofit donor deck. Oswald is best at tightly knit, confident display rows, while Andada Pro is best at gentle stroke shifts and counters that welcome the eye.
curated-fs-oswald-gf-anta: Wire-bent sign energy: Oswald packs tight, confident rows while sans-serif Anta draws its lines at constant thickness. The standout is Anta's flat, contrast-free build, down to its gaping-mouthed e.
curated-fs-oswald-gf-antic: Tall, tight and sure of itself, Oswald sits over a body that looks traced with one marker nib. Antic keeps long reading moving, its open letter mouths leaving a light, professional feel.
curated-fs-oswald-gf-ar-one-sans: Oswald packs its letters into tightly knit, confident rows. AR One Sans lifts its brush-like ends away before curves close, giving that dense heading a lighter sans companion beneath.
curated-fs-oswald-gf-chathura: Chathura reads compressed and quick, like thin steel rod bent into letters. Oswald above it is just as tight but strong and display-minded, so the two feel like related cuts of one metal.
curated-fs-oswald-gf-harmattan: Oswald packs its rows of text tightly and speaks with confidence. Harmattan's sans strokes stay monoline from stem to terminal, fine for, say, a bakery badge logo, though large body text would swamp Oswald.
curated-fs-oswald-gf-rationale: Confident Oswald packs its rows tight up top (think a school crest), while Rationale below keeps its letters bunched with tiny gaps. That sans body is better kept brief, not stretched over pages.
curated-fs-oswald-gf-share-tech-mono: Typewriter-steady and precise, the monospace body gives each letter equal width beneath confident Oswald. Share Tech Mono is happiest with a few words, say a yoga logo, rather than whole pages.
curated-fs-panchang-author: Author reads refined and dignified, with a slight swell on its bowls. Panchang is best at wide, open, steady display lines, while Author's measured weight does its finest work in a few lines of text.
curated-fs-panchang-bitter: Bitter brings a slab-serif body with a very large lowercase and see-through s shapes (handy for boat and marine work). Panchang is best at flat, unmodulated strokes with generous space, while Bitter does its best at grounded, sturdy text.
curated-fs-pencerio-gf-andada-pro: A formal, clenched calligraphic hand leads the way. Pencerio excels at graceful, tightly fitted words, while Andada Pro offers serif counters the eye can slip in and out of.
curated-fs-pencerio-gf-bona-nova-sc: Bona Nova SC reads refined, its small counters unclogged and its serif strokes gently shaded. Its best quality is a lightly textured softness that lets Pencerio's formal, closely fitted script stand apart above it.
curated-fs-pencerio-gf-gulzar: Graceful Pencerio could head a concierge service sign, its formal calligraphic words tightly fitted. Gulzar gives a text serif authority through lightly swelling curves, best kept to brief stretches.
curated-fs-pencerio-gf-lustria: Pencerio's clenched calligraphy could headline an employee of the month card. Lustria, a classic serif, holds traditional authority through weight changes that never turn dramatic, so keep it to brief lines.
curated-fs-pencerio-gf-maname: Pencerio's clenched, calligraphic words feel formal and graceful (think a luxury real estate flyer). Maname, a classic serif with horizontals slimmer than its verticals, is bookish and editorial, pleasant in modest helpings.
curated-fs-pencerio-gf-mate: Mate reads dignified and editorial, its round letters looking cupped. Pencerio's clenched script heading is formal, so give Mate a generous size and its lighter horizontals will hold up across a few lines.
curated-fs-pencerio-gf-nanum-myeongjo: Nanum Myeongjo reads refined and editorial, its curve tips left open. Pencerio's graceful, clenched script takes the spotlight while the classic serif beneath keeps medium contrast, ideal for a few lines.
curated-fs-pencerio-gf-noto-serif-hk: Clenched, closely fitted calligraphy gives Pencerio a graceful, formal look at a glance (a wedding program, say). Pencerio makes the entrance; Noto Serif HK does the reading, in modest doses.
curated-fs-pencerio-gf-noto-serif-jp: Graceful and formal, Pencerio clenches its calligraphy into tight words. Noto Serif JP, a classic serif with an unclenched c, reads literary and refined, though only across brief spans.
curated-fs-pencerio-gf-noto-serif-tangut: A calligraphic hand with tightly clenched word shapes defines Pencerio. Pencerio does graceful formality best, while Noto Serif Tangut handles literary, traditional text with restrained thick-thin play, good in compact bursts.
curated-fs-pencerio-gf-petrona: Petrona's shallow terminal curls and tempered contrast might label a set of table numbers. Petrona lets Pencerio's graceful, calligraphic hand lead, then carries brief spans of text beneath it.
curated-fs-pencerio-gf-poly: Pencerio is a clenched, calligraphic script with closely fitted words. Poly adds a bookish, literary voice with gently thinning bowls, and a touch more size helps it hold brief spans.
curated-fs-pencerio-gf-quattrocento: Quattrocento keeps its lines slim and its curves open. Pencerio's calligraphic hand sits above it, tightly clenched and formal, while the body below stays light, like etched lines in glass.
curated-fs-pencerio-gf-vollkorn: Formal Pencerio brings a clenched calligraphic hand (nail salon identity, say) to the top of the page. And Vollkorn, literary and faintly modulated, welcomes a slightly larger size, happiest in brief doses.
curated-fs-pencerio-gf-vollkorn-sc: Pencerio writes in a clenched, calligraphic hand with tightly fitted words. It handles the flourish and formality up top, leaving Vollkorn SC to supply the dignified, literary text serif with its loosely tracked, medium-contrast strokes.
curated-fs-pencerio-libre-baskerville: Refined and bookish, Libre Baskerville stretches sideways beneath the script. Pencerio's tight, graceful hand makes a short stop, whereas this text serif's modest thick-thin shift would grow tiring across many paragraphs.
curated-fs-pramukh-rounded-fs-erode: Pramukh Rounded packs its letters shoulder to shoulder, barely a gap between them. Use it big and brief, while Erode, the serif below, ebbs and flows in stroke weight and keeps its horizontals light but never threadlike.
curated-fs-pramukh-rounded-gf-atkinson-h: Pramukh Rounded crowds its glyphs close, with bowls tipped open like a ladle. Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono spreads wide in answer, and over a long stretch its roomy counters let the text breathe.
curated-fs-pramukh-rounded-gf-funnel-san: Pramukh Rounded runs its large lowercase tight and friendly, with hardly any gap between glyphs, and Funnel Sans follows below it. Over a long passage, the plain sans keeps every stroke at a steady width.
curated-fs-pramukh-rounded-gf-noto-sans-: Tightly bunched glyphs mark Pramukh Rounded, a friendly choice for a number counting book, say. And Noto Sans Lisu can go a touch larger, since its tiny ascender gaps and wide s curves stay easy on the eye.
curated-fs-pramukh-rounded-gf-vend-sans: Vend Sans draws a ruler-straight line with wide, unclosed curve endings and a tall x-height. Pramukh Rounded crowds its glyphs tight above it, and the shared friendly softness would suit, for instance, a name poster for a child.
curated-fs-quilon-bitter: Dependable and grounded, Bitter shows a very large lowercase eye and a see-through gap in each s. Quilon's display letters above it carry a faint nib-pressure swell, and the slab-serif body can stay at a modest size.
curated-fs-quilon-gf-grenze: Editorial Quilon, with its calm ebb and flow of stroke, could front a yoga logo without strain. But Grenze, tall and dignified with small sidebearings, is better for brief lines than pages.
curated-fs-quilon-roboto-slab: Quilon swells and thins in a soft, unhurried step from heavy to light. Roboto Slab follows with a sturdy, slab-serif body whose dominant middle zone makes a long stretch of text feel firmly structured and easy to trust.
curated-fs-rajdhani-gf-alegreya-sc: Rajdhani is all uniform strokes, with text packed into dense, tightly woven strips. Alegreya SC adds a traditional, authoritative voice through gently thinning curves, comfortable enough for a grocery list.
curated-fs-rajdhani-gf-arapey: Modern and clean, Rajdhani keeps every line flat like a fineliner. Arapey's strength is the drama inside each letter, a heavy trunk with whisper-thin branches, which makes a handful of lines look polished.
curated-fs-rajdhani-gf-bacasime-antique: Crisp, uniform strokes up top, then a serif with heavy verticals and hairline connections. Rajdhani keeps the headline sharp while Bacasime Antique brings an authoritative editorial weight, and its tight clustering is not meant for long paragraphs.
curated-fs-rajdhani-gf-diphylleia: Pen-plotter smooth, Rajdhani packs its text into dense strips. Rajdhani excels at crisp, modern headings, whereas Diphylleia, a text serif, does better with bookish paragraphs where stems outweigh hairlines a little.
curated-fs-rajdhani-gf-libertinus-serif: Libertinus Serif carries a slight swell in its bowls and an open s, which lends it a refined, authoritative voice. Libertinus Serif does the steady paragraph work, while Rajdhani is happiest as a modern, tightly woven headline.
curated-fs-rajdhani-gf-nanum-myeongjo: Nanum Myeongjo is a refined text serif with open curve tips. Its quiet stroke modulation keeps a full page of reading editorial and unhurried, while Rajdhani stays modern and clean on top.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-baskervville: Marker-bold lines with daylight in every curve lead the way here. Red Hat Display is best at bold, constant-width statements, while Baskervville, with its small low-set lowercase and hairline crossbars, is best at graceful text.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-fs-recia: Red Hat Display cuts its curves like a fixed-width router bit, bold and contemporary, with daylight inside every bend. Recia then reads sharp and authoritative, its gentle thick-thin rhythm easing along.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-abel: Abel reads close-set and unfussy, beads on a thread with horseshoe-open apertures, the sort you might meet in a terminal theme. Red Hat Display adds marker-bold lines with daylight inside every curve.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-alegreya-s: Alegreya Sans has a broad g and a, with letters squeezed close, under a marker-plain Red Hat Display. Alegreya Sans keeps a long block of text steady and friendly, maybe beside a coffee roaster logo.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-assistant: Red Hat Display draws every letter with one width of stroke, like a bent wire, bold and contemporary. And Assistant keeps its mouths open below, so its size can stay modest for, say, demo video title cards.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-asul: Red Hat Display has dowel-like stems and bent arcs, bold enough for, say, a boutique hotel logo. Asul handles the low-key thick-thin variation, leaving the uniform strokes to the heading.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-b612: Marker-like strokes, contemporary and bold, with daylight inside every curve. Red Hat Display carries that boldness at size, while B612, a plain-spoken sans with a low lowercase, stays approachable beneath it.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-belleza: Bent-wire lettering over a body with a gentle weight gradient and tiny gaps between glyphs. Shrink Red Hat Display and its bold character fades, while Belleza at large sizes shows its slivers of space.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-castoro: A blunt, round-tip marker feel runs end to end in Red Hat Display. Castoro, a dignified text serif, pits heavy strokes against thread-thin ones, a tension best enjoyed over a paragraph or two.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-gloock: Wire-bent curves that never thin, say, on an esports team logo. Red Hat Display holds the line steady while Gloock, with its bold-and-fine strokes, adds dignified drama to a few words.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-playfair: Dignified, with a pale thread running between black stems. Red Hat Display does plain, constant-width boldness best, while Playfair does the thick-and-hairline contrast, maybe for an accounting firm wordmark.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-pt-sans-na: Tightly kerned and approachable, the body text is made for brief bursts (a law firm monogram, for instance). PT Sans Narrow keeps stroke widths constant, while Red Hat Display does its best work as the bold, contemporary heading.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-tiro-devan: Bold marker lines with matching curves and stems lead the way (a food truck logo, say), and Tiro Devanagari Hindi follows. Give Red Hat Display the size and let the serif stay modest.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-tiro-tamil: Red Hat Display runs marker-bold (a bakery badge logo, say). Beside it, Tiro Tamil sets heavy slanted strokes against thread-thin partners, a dignified serif made for brief spells of reading.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-voltaire: A marker-like constant line gives Red Hat Display its daylight-filled curves, handy for a fitness wordmark. And Voltaire keeps its glyphs tightly fitted, a compact partner that fits a line or two more than long paragraphs.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-wdxl-lubri: Red Hat Display speaks up with marker-bold lines and open curves. WDXL Lubrifont TC trails it in tight felt-tip strokes, holding its width through every turn and happiest in a few words.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-zen-antiqu: Cut like sign-shop vinyl at a single line width, Red Hat Display looks bold and modern. Zen Antique answers with fat black stems and chalk-dust serifs, a literary weight that suits brief stretches of reading.
curated-fs-rosaline-gf-im-fell-english-s: Rosaline writes in flowing pen strokes, heavy timber beside fine wire, with its c nearly closed. And IM Fell English SC takes the moderate path, open-throated and bookish, better for text than for long paragraphs.
curated-fs-rosaline-gf-inria-sans: A pale thread running between two black stems marks Rosaline as the showpiece, luxurious and understated. And Inria Sans, tubular like bent copper pipe, can stay modest in size (a baby shower invitation would leave it there).
curated-fs-rosaline-gf-jura: Rosaline writes in closed, pen-flowing letters with sharp bright edges. Jura sits below in wire-constant strokes and wide-open s curves, so the page moves from ornate to plain, comfortable in small doses.
curated-fs-rosaline-gf-kosugi-maru: Kosugi Maru reads like neon tubing, with one steady line and stroke ends set far apart. Its open letters give Rosaline's heavy verticals and paper-thin horizontals something clear to lean against, made for short stretches of reading.
curated-fs-rosaline-gf-libre-caslon-text: Libre Caslon Text reads refined and editorial, say a wedding menu. The serif keeps a middling thick-thin contrast that moves along gently, while Rosaline pairs fat strokes with hairlines.
curated-fs-rosaline-gf-marcellus: Luxurious hairline flourishes lead in Rosaline, flowing like pen-written letters with sharp bright edges against fat darkness. Marcellus follows with subtle, etched weight changes, better for brief copy.
curated-fs-rosaline-gf-mate-sc: Mate SC sits low and dignified, its round letters faintly pressed. Rosaline's closed script forms flow above it, so give the Mate SC text a size generous enough for its open curves to breathe.
curated-fs-rosaline-gf-noto-serif-jp: Luxurious and understated, Rosaline writes closed, flowing letters, for instance on a bar mitzvah invitation. And Noto Serif JP loosens things below with open, steady letters whose thins never turn spindly, better for brief text.
curated-fs-rosaline-gf-peddana: Sharp edges against fat darkness: Rosaline writes with a flowing pen. Peddana sits tight and dense underneath, drawn with a barely tilted nib, so it handles a couple of lines gracefully beside those threadlike tails.
curated-fs-rosaline-gf-petrona: Rosaline is all luxury: hairlines that nearly vanish beside fat, dark strokes. Petrona, a text serif with a soft gradient of weight, reads gently and fits brief stretches best.
curated-fs-rosaline-gf-radley: Radley lets the eye slip in and out of its counters, with robust downstrokes and slender turns. Rosaline is best at closed, flowing flourish, while Radley's strength is open, dignified text.
curated-fs-rosaline-gf-roboto-serif: Luxurious and understated, Rosaline looks carved from ink and thread (a vow booklet, say). Roboto Serif does the quieter job, with generous open eyes and well-spaced letters, ideal in brief spells.
curated-fs-rosaline-gf-sawarabi-mincho: Flowing and luxurious: Rosaline swings from fat strokes to hairlines, with sharp bright edges against deep darkness. Sawarabi Mincho, with gently easing joins, reads steadily across a few lines.
curated-fs-rosaline-gf-shippori-mincho-b: Shippori Mincho B1 opens its c like a crescent wrench, with hairlines of reasonable sturdiness. Rosaline's stout pillars and fine threads sit above, closed and ornate against that open, sturdy serif.
curated-fs-rosaline-gf-sura: Sura reads traditional and authoritative, its hairlines slightly thin and its terminals never closing in. Rosaline, closed and razor-fine, wants generous size, for instance on a bachelorette invitation, while Sura takes brief bursts.
curated-fs-rx-100-gf-alumni-sans-pinstri: Alumni Sans Pinstripe reads tight and friendly, maybe beside an indie game logo. RX100 crowds zero-contrast letters into a futuristic block, while the pinstripe body pairs oversized lowercase with small capitals, good for a line or two.
curated-fs-rx-100-gf-cousine: Technical and tidy, Cousine lays out fixed-width monospace letters with tall lowercase. RX100 stays tight and contrast-free above it, and both feel built from a machine, which would suit a slide deck for tech talk.
curated-fs-segment-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Pilcrow Rounded packs its letters tightly, with big counters and curves left unclosed. Segment above it spreads out instead, with generous gaps and a stocky middle band, so the two push in opposite directions on the page.
curated-fs-segment-gf-alumni-sans: Alumni Sans keeps its ascenders low and its c wide open, a fit for a tabletop rpg book if you like. Alumni Sans gives Segment's stocky, widely spaced letters a lighter partner with only a slight thinning at the curves.
curated-fs-segment-gf-judson: Judson reads dignified and bookish, with brushlike curve endings and bulky small letters. Segment stands above in stocky, spaced-out capitals with little stroke variation, while Judson's swelling and thinning strokes bring the warmth beneath it.
curated-fs-segment-gf-noto-serif-sinhala: Refined and bookish, Noto Serif Sinhala would sit well in a barbershop emblem, with its tall letters and lively strokes. Segment is the one for commanding, spacious headings; Noto Serif Sinhala is the one for quieter text with moderate contrast.
curated-fs-stardom-gf-fira-code: Fira Code runs precise and technical, a code editor font at heart. Stardom's fat-to-fine swings make the heading dramatic, so give Fira Code a size comfortable enough to show off its open channels between letters.
curated-fs-stardom-gf-noto-serif-grantha: Noto Serif Grantha reads refined and classic, its small letters oversized and its contrast tempered. Stardom brings chunky stems and filament-thin connectors above it, and that sharp jump from the body's gentle arches is the pair's real draw.
curated-fs-striper-gf-noto-znamenny-musi: Noto Znamenny Musical Notation stays clean, terminals stopping far from the stem. Striper does the loud, playful graphic work (say, a gender reveal party), while the notation font handles quiet, comfortable reading.
curated-fs-styro-gf-alexandria: Retro and commanding, Styro crowds its big lowercase so tightly that the letters nearly close up. Alexandria does the opposite job best, with open terminals and a tall body that make running text easy to follow.
curated-fs-styro-gf-victor-mono: Victor Mono sets its monospace letters loosely, with bowls left open on one side and a size that looks magnified. Bump its size up a notch against Styro's crowded retro heading.
curated-fs-styro-montserrat: Styro brings a retro, crowded swagger, with letters jammed nearly shut (handy for an art deco invitation, say). And Montserrat glides along below it, round and geometric, with plenty of white space leading into each curve.
curated-fs-tanker-fs-paquito: Tanker turns every open curve inward and packs its letters tight, with lowercase that looks huge beside the capitals. Give Tanker large sizes; Paquito, a confident serif, is not for whole pages.
curated-fs-telma-archivo: Flowing pen-written Telma, thin strokes about half the weight of thick ones, sits above Archivo, whose curves open outward. The body carries the sentences; the script is happiest with a few words.
curated-fs-telma-gf-anek-latin: Anek Latin stands tall, its lowercase nearly reaching the capitals, with curves held open beneath the flowing pen-written Telma. Reading feels brisk and tidy, fitting a quick bit of text.
curated-fs-telma-gf-anek-telugu: Pulled-taffy swells in Telma meet wide, tall bowls in Anek Telugu. The body font reads with a clear, friendly rhythm, but it is not built for pages of dense text.
curated-fs-telma-gf-arimo: Graceful and understated, Telma writes with a pen's flow. Arimo echoes that high mean line and keeps its rounded terminals spacious, a steady partner built for quick reading.
curated-fs-telma-gf-armata: Understated Telma script could front a seed packet, wide-mouthed and pen-written. Armata, a sans-serif with spacious gaps between characters, works when the words are few, though a shrunken Telma would lose its high, flowing line.
curated-fs-telma-gf-arsenal: Arsenal keeps its sans-serif letters close-knit, with a x-height nearly matching the caps. Next to Telma's flowing pen script, it feels grounded and brisk, a quiet foil to all that graceful movement.
curated-fs-telma-gf-atkinson-hyperlegibl: Telma writes graceful, pen-made letters with sturdy hairlines, while Atkinson Hyperlegible keeps its capitals clipped and its s terminals wide-set. Reading flows smoothly, though the pair likes only a few words.
curated-fs-telma-gf-bayon: Bayon reads approachable and tight-knit, its round o's holding a constant wall all the way around. And the pair's real hook is Telma's modest thick-thin shift against curves that never swell, which favors brief wording.
curated-fs-telma-gf-carlito: Telma writes with a faint nib-pressure swell across each round letter. Carlito, tight-spaced and clear at small sizes, keeps things readable, though it would wear thin over long paragraphs (a welcome drink card is plenty).
curated-fs-telma-gf-carrois-gothic-sc: Graceful Telma writes flowing letters under a high mean line, with a middling contrast like a half-turned flat brush. Carrois Gothic SC keeps every curve open, so brief lines suit it best.
curated-fs-telma-gf-farro: Farro draws a tube-like stroke with compressed ascenders. Telma handles the flowing pen-written grace while Farro supplies unvarying strokes, pleasant in brief moments such as a wedding menu.
curated-fs-telma-gf-fira-code: Telma's flowing, pen-written letters ride a high mean line and open wide in the a. Fira Code, a precise monospace with open channels between letters, handles a few words well, giving the script a technical counterweight.
curated-fs-telma-gf-fjalla-one: Fjalla One packs tight lowercase that could front a jam jar label. Telma's open, flowing letters against that closed, tight body make a sharp difference, and a couple of lines is plenty.
curated-fs-telma-gf-hammersmith-one: A high mean line runs through every word of Telma. Hammersmith One's rounded, cord-like strokes hold steady beside the soft-pencil shifts of Telma, and the pair is built for brief reading.
curated-fs-telma-gf-homenaje: Telma writes with thin strokes half the weight of its thick ones. Flow is what Telma does best, while Homenaje, with its tall middle zone and close-knit spacing, is best kept off lengthy text.
curated-fs-telma-gf-huninn: Telma writes in flowing pen strokes, maybe for a stock certificate. Where Telma flows with middle-ground contrast, Huninn holds a monoweight stroke and lowercase rising near cap height, made for text kept brief.
curated-fs-telma-gf-khula: Hairline to stem: Telma swells in measured steps. Khula, with its tall midsection and curves that hold their mouths open, sits quietly beside it, made for text that stays short.
curated-fs-telma-gf-kufam: Kufam runs one stroke width through the whole alphabet. Against Telma's mild shimmer of changing weight, that single track looks like a neon sign tube, good for a quick line or two.
curated-fs-telma-gf-league-gothic: Tall and tightly packed, League Gothic reads like a column of fence posts. Telma's open, flowing script gives it room to breathe, so the heading drifts above the cramped sans, built for brief reading.
curated-fs-telma-gf-liter: Liter keeps every stroke, the g included, at a single weight. Liter's tall lowercase stands steady under Telma's shaded, flowing heading (a fit for an ex libris bookplate, maybe), best for brief spells of text.
curated-fs-telma-gf-miriam-libre: Soft pen-written script meets wire-weight lettering in Miriam Libre, an approachable modern body. Telma thins its bowls gracefully above that cast-iron lowercase, and the combination is built for brief reads.
curated-fs-telma-gf-mochiy-pop-one: Mochiy Pop One, a sans-serif, would suit, say, a desk nameplate. Its oversized lowercase eye and unvarying weight read steadily, while Telma stays approachable; short text suits it best.
curated-fs-telma-gf-momo-signature: Momo Signature lets its lowercase rival the capitals in height. Telma's open letterforms flow above while the body keeps its crimped, closed-in gaps, a contrast that stays pleasant in tiny portions.
curated-fs-telma-gf-mukta-vaani: Contemporary and high-waisted, Mukta Vaani barely modulates any stroke. Under Telma's subtly modulated script, the body text moves along quite smoothly, though it is happiest in modest portions of text.
curated-fs-telma-gf-noto-rashi-hebrew: Bookish and lightly engraved, Noto Rashi Hebrew reads like brass lettering, with short ascender stems on bodies that stand tall. Telma adds flowing script above, best for brief stretches.
curated-fs-telma-gf-noto-sans-adlam-unjo: Crisp and spacious, Noto Sans Adlam Unjoined leaves generous gaps between curve ends and stems, with little height difference between cases. Telma's in-between shading keeps the text gentle, if taken sparingly.
curated-fs-telma-gf-noto-sans-avestan: Noto Sans Avestan reads clean and modern, with a pronounced x-height. Beside Telma's felt-marker swelling, text runs on crisply, though it's made for brief reading, a business card for instance.
curated-fs-telma-gf-noto-sans-elymaic: Graceful Telma writes its headings in flowing pen strokes, with a wide-mouthed a. Noto Sans Elymaic follows in open, clean shapes whose ascenders barely rise above the x-height, so lines stay low and steady.
curated-fs-telma-gf-noto-sans-gothic: Noto Sans Gothic has huge round counters, like open parentheses. Telma's flowing script above it keeps its contrast moderate, so the two feel understated and modern at once, never fighting for attention.
curated-fs-telma-gf-noto-sans-lao-looped: Noto Sans Lao Looped sets words as solid blocks, bowls left open. Telma leads with flat-brush contrast and graceful pen strokes (think of a memorial service invitation), and the body keeps quick reading comfortable.
curated-fs-telma-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Noto Sans Limbu reads wide and gaping, with tall-bodied small letters. Beside Telma and its graceful pen-written lead, that openness stands out most, and the pair is made for brief reading.
curated-fs-telma-gf-noto-sans-mandaic: Telma's pen-written letters sit under a high mean line, flowing across each word. Make the heading small and that thread-like contrast fades, while Noto Sans Mandaic's lowercase, rising close to capitals, stays curvy and readable.
curated-fs-telma-gf-noto-sans-tai-viet: Approachable and quick to read, Noto Sans Tai Viet has short ascenders and a tall x-height. Telma is the one for flowing script with a wide a, while the body handles the steady text work.
curated-fs-telma-gf-noto-sans-tamil: Contemporary in feel, Noto Sans Tamil looks magnified even at normal size, with terminals stopping far from the stem. Across a long passage it reads generously, and Telma's slightly thin hairlines add a graceful flourish (a certificate of achievement, say).
curated-fs-telma-gf-noto-serif-balinese: Noto Serif Balinese brings traditional, editorial weight, with lowercase that stands tall. Telma does the graceful handwriting up top, while the serif carries the text with a comfortable midpoint between flat and dramatic strokes.
curated-fs-telma-gf-noto-serif-khojki: Noto Serif Khojki, refined and literary, could quietly set a wedding menu in short ascenders above big bowls. Telma excels at flowing, pen-written headings, while the serif excels at gentle, low-key thick-thin variation in its text.
curated-fs-telma-gf-noto-serif-lao: Telma's wide-mouthed a and high mean line give its script an understated, hand-written grace. Noto Serif Lao answers with authority, its big lowercase and gently shifting bowls making the pair feel bookish yet light.
curated-fs-telma-gf-noto-serif-vithkuqi: Telma's flowing, pen-written letters under a high mean line lean graceful, while Noto Serif Vithkuqi brings big round lowercase bowls. Editorial in tone, it reads comfortably across a few lines.
curated-fs-telma-gf-noto-serif-yezidi: Noto Serif Yezidi sets words as solid blocks, with strokes that taper gently. Telma brings flowing, pen-written letters under a high mean line, and the pair is happiest with brief copy rather than endless pages.
curated-fs-telma-gf-orienta: Orienta breathes easily, with counters like a hollow reed cut open. Telma is best at graceful, pen-written flourish, while Orienta's modern build keeps capitals and lowercase near in height, so long paragraphs are out.
curated-fs-telma-gf-radio-canada: Telma's pen-written letters flow beneath a high mean line. Radio Canada, a sans-serif with unstressed curves and clear openings, backs it up on the page whenever the reading is quick.
curated-fs-telma-gf-stack-sans-headline: Telma suits, say, a wedding website, with graceful pen-written letters. Stack Sans Headline, a monoline sans with wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp, carries the quick reading while Telma's gentle modulation never snags the eye.
curated-fs-telma-gf-voces: Voces reads tall and crisp, its stems and hairlines close in weight. Telma does its best work as a graceful, pen-written script with a high mean line, while Voces is built for steady, clear text.
curated-fs-telma-gf-winky-rough: Winky Rough stands tall, its lowercase nearly matching the capitals. Telma's brushy, pen-written flow adds grace, but across many lines the sans body tires fast, so keep it away from long paragraphs.
curated-fs-zina-lora: Sharp and dramatic, Zina swings from fat strokes to hairlines, while Lora keeps a broad, welcoming c, handy for a bookshop logo. Lora reads like a literary serif, though not for long paragraphs.
curated-fugaz-one-gf-david-libre: Bent-paperclip energy, that's Fugaz One, with narrow letter margins. David Libre, a dignified serif with terminals that hang open, settles things down, and works well on a small cluster of lines.
curated-gf-aboreto-gf-imbue: Aboreto stands wide and commanding, its stems thick with hairline crossbars. Imbue underneath is snug and moderate in contrast, with a very large lowercase that makes paragraphs feel dense and dignified.
curated-gf-acme-fs-erode: Wire-bent and upright, Acme holds one constant line width across tall strokes and short rounded bodies. Erode's serif then adds a tall middle band and gentle weight shifts, softening the page with an editorial hush.
curated-gf-agu-display-gf-science-gothic: Distinctive, loopy and bold: Agu Display bends its strokes like thin plastic tubing. Science Gothic keeps every letter uniform in weight and its stroke ends far apart, so give that sans a little extra size.
curated-gf-aguafina-script-gf-red-hat-mo: Tall strokes over short, rounded bodies give Aguafina Script a compact, personal hand. Red Hat Mono, a technical monospace with long beats between letters, ticks along steadily, though it is happiest when the text is brief.
curated-gf-akaya-kanadaka-space-grotesk: Space Grotesk draws every glyph as a ribbon of constant width, with counters that breathe like a hollow reed. Akaya Kanadaka adds tight spacing and pulled-back terminals, both made for quick reads.
curated-gf-akaya-telivigala-gf-noto-sans: Noto Sans Linear A gaps its c visibly at any size, a clean foil for a poster print shop merch headline in Akaya Telivigala. And that heading crowds its glyphs like beads on a wire.
curated-gf-akronim-gf-bhutuka-expanded-o: Akronim snags its curves and clamps seams tight, closed and bold. BhuTuka Expanded One, a serif, slows the pace to a stroll with curvy, open letters, so the heading shouts while the body talks.
curated-gf-akronim-gf-inconsolata: Inconsolata is monospace, with a c shaped like a wide ring. Akronim's bold, closed, tightly seamed letters against that open, fixed-width structure is the best trick here, comfortable for brief reading.
curated-gf-alkatra-gf-biorhyme-expanded: BioRhyme Expanded reads bookish and wide, every word breaking into single letters with open gaps. And Alkatra does bold display best, hairlines present but not razor thin, while the serif body does best on brief text.
curated-gf-allan-fs-roundo: Tight, bold, expressive: Allan hugs its letters together, its y tail matching its arm. Roundo takes the quieter job, with unclogged small counters and an n matched arch to stem, pleasant in modest amounts.
curated-gf-allura-zilla-slab: Zilla Slab reads sturdy and technical, fine for general purpose use. Allura does graceful, friendly handwriting best, its strokes one stylus wide, while the slab's broad open curves are happiest on brief lines.
curated-gf-alumni-sans-inline-one-gf-not: Expressive heavy downstrokes and cobweb-fine upstrokes make Alumni Sans Inline One loud and narrow. Noto Serif Balinese settles things with gentle stroke variation and great vertical presence, better suited to brief text.
curated-gf-alumni-sans-inline-one-noto-s: Noto Serif reads with a literary hush and a prominent x-height. Its gentle cadence carries text along, while Alumni Sans Inline One brings swollen curves to, say, a dark fantasy game title.
curated-gf-amarante-gf-bhutuka-expanded-: BhuTuka Expanded One slows to a leisurely walk beneath Amarante. Curvy, unclamped letters and joins no thinner than the stems feel literary, though lengthy paragraphs would be asking too much.
