gen-dm-serif-display-gf-cascadia-mono: DM Serif Display drops heavy downstrokes beside ghostlike upstrokes, giving headings a dignified, authoritative pull. And Cascadia Mono keeps a single line weight, compact and modern, its letters standing like pins in a board.
gen-dm-serif-display-montserrat: DM Serif Display swings from heavy to hairline inside every letter, which gives headings a dignified, authoritative edge. Montserrat just glides, a sans line with no modulation at all.
gen-dm-serif-text-fs-public-sans: Heavy stems joined by thread-thin arms give DM Serif Text a bookish, editorial bite right away. And Public Sans, a hefty sans-serif with broad open counters, settles in underneath with trustworthy, low-key weight.
gen-dm-serif-text-fs-synonym: DM Serif Text mixes thick bars with hairline strokes for an editorial, bookish voice. And Synonym, drawn like a bent steel rod, reads comfortably a size or two below the heading.
gen-dm-serif-text-space-grotesk: Swollen, brush-pressed stems beside hairline arms make DM Serif Text unmistakably bookish. Space Grotesk would carry a lengthy block of text smoothly, its open counters and constant-width strokes leaving no hairlines to catch on.
gen-eater-fs-fira-sans: Eater is dark and aggressive, with wide gaps between letters and short ascenders. Fira Sans, with one stroke thickness throughout and a larger-than-usual x-height, can be sized modestly and still read clearly.
gen-fascinate-fs-rowan: Rowan reads friendly and bookish, with generous openings in every curve. Fascinate earns its keep when it's big and brief, its widely spaced letters pairing fat verticals with hair-thin diagonals.
gen-flavors-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Flavors is whimsical and commanding, with a towering x-height. Flavors does its best work shouting, while Be Vietnam Pro does its best work keeping curve endings well apart on a high mean line.
gen-flavors-fs-hind: Hind keeps its lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals. Flavors is the one to shout with, towering and whimsical, while Hind does the steady work, its curve ends never turning inward.
gen-flavors-fs-paquito: Paquito sounds confident and approachable, with caps barely taller than its lowercase. Over pages of text it should feel friendly and unhurried, while Flavors, thick as neon glass tubing, stays out front as the loud one.
gen-flavors-fs-quicksand: A towering x-height, like a stubby pencil stroke, defines Flavors. Quicksand takes over below with bulb-round lowercase and uniform bar thickness, so the loud heading and gentle body feel related.
gen-flavors-gf-abyssinica-sil: Flavors looks drawn with a single nib, whimsical and commanding, its diagonals matching its stems. And Abyssinica SIL softens it with a gentle ebb and flow of stroke thickness, tall through the middle of every word.
gen-flavors-gf-atkinson-hyperlegible-nex: Whimsical and commanding, Flavors draws every stroke like thick wire. Atkinson Hyperlegible Next sits beneath with big-eyed lowercase and open rounds, so the page moves from shout to easy conversation.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: Flavors keeps its strokes free of any swelling or thinning. Noto Sans Ol Chiki holds its curve tails back and packs words into solid blocks, so the loud heading gets a tidy counterpart.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-thaana: Flavors gives every stroke equal visual weight, diagonals included, and lifts a towering x-height like a stubby pencil stroke. Noto Sans Thaana has wide channels, so a generous size suits it.
gen-flavors-gf-piazzolla: Piazzolla reads refined and authoritative, its lowercase nearly matching the capitals. Page after page it should hold steady and dignified, while Flavors, cut like laser sheet with a single stroke width, supplies the shouting.
gen-flavors-gf-savate: Soft, cheeky, stubby-pencil letters from Flavors sit up top. Savate runs on sturdy hairlines and open curves, so paragraphs of it keep moving without tiring the eye for long.
gen-flavors-rubik: Flavors goes big and bossy, with a towering x-height and no shading. Rubik does the quiet work, its soft round letters staying legible even when set small and its lowercase looking generous next to the capitals.
gen-fraunces-archivo: Lightly engraved brass lettering, dignified and a little bookish. Fraunces is best at modest contrast and generously opened curves, while Archivo is best at lowercase height that commands the line.
gen-fraunces-fs-public-sans: Trustworthy, first of all, and a touch bookish too: Fraunces writes like a dip pen used gently. Public Sans follows with a hefty lowercase, so it can be sized modestly and still hold its ground.
gen-fraunces-fs-spline-sans: Spline Sans reads flat and friendly, with unmodulated strokes and generous gaps where curves meet the stems. Long paragraphs would glide along smoothly, with Fraunces holding the dignified top.
gen-fraunces-space-grotesk: Dignified Fraunces leads with generous curve openings and gently varied line weight. And Space Grotesk, drawn at the width of one stylus, carries a long paragraph without a stumble.
gen-fraunces-work-sans: Fraunces opens up every curve terminal, giving its moderate contrast a gentle taper from stem to joint. Work Sans then runs a marker-like constant line with a high mean line, so a long page feels crisp and modern.
gen-fredoka-fs-alpino: Alpino is cozy and casual, with a very tall body and curve endings kept well apart. Fredoka does friendly with its single-width pen line, while Alpino does the quiet part of keeping text close and compact.
gen-fredoka-fs-bespoke-sans: Bespoke Sans looks sharp and refined, with generous space at each curve end. A long passage in it reads crisp and orderly, a nice foil to Fredoka's round, friendly heading.
gen-fredoka-fs-bespoke-serif: Bespoke Serif brings authority, its thin strokes about half the weight of thick ones. Fredoka's uniform, friendly line sits above it, and the wedge-like pressure in the serif's curves gives the pair a pleasing bite.
gen-fredoka-general-sans: Fredoka holds a single pen width from stem to curve. The heading is the approachable voice up top, while General Sans, a sans with a lowercase that fills the line, slides smoothly around every bend.
gen-fredoka-gf-graduate: Soft and bookish at once: Fredoka's single-width line meets Graduate, a serif with generous space between its letters. Friendly openness up top, and a dignified, spaced-out serif settling in beneath.
gen-fredoka-gf-lisu-bosa: Round, friendly, and drawn with one steady line. Fredoka keeps the top light and approachable, while Lisu Bosa's tall, sturdy lowercase gives the text beneath it an editorial footing.
gen-fredoka-gf-noto-serif-hentaigana: Fredoka keeps a friendly single-width line and an open e. Noto Serif Hentaigana, a serif with open jaws on every curved stroke and small letters nearly as tall as capitals, is where the real difference lives.
gen-fs-alpino-fs-erode: Felt-tip friendly, Alpino stands tall and generous in every weight. Erode, with a tall middle band and a gentle ebb of stroke weight, keeps paragraphs moving with dignified, unhurried ease.
gen-fs-array-fs-ranade: Ranade reads loose and spread-out, its stroke ends far apart. Array, futuristic and precise, brings large lowercase eyes up top, and the pairing feels made for quick visits rather than marathons.
gen-fs-azeret-mono-fs-karma: Azeret Mono sets every letter in a fixed-width, code-style slot. Karma, a serif with a mild taper and lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals, lets text glide along without snagging the eye.
gen-fs-azeret-mono-fs-public-sans: Technical and functional, Azeret Mono spaces its fixed-width letters generously. Public Sans, a sans with a hefty lowercase and broad counters, fills in the body while the monospace heading stays crisp up top.
gen-fs-azeret-mono-fs-ranade: Azeret Mono lays out fixed-width, code-style letters with generous tracking that opens each word. Ranade, with slightly shifting weight and widely spaced type, then loosens the body text to match.
gen-fs-azeret-mono-instrument-sans: Azeret Mono locks its code-style letters into fixed-width slots, with generous tracking between them. And Instrument Sans, with one unvarying stroke weight and a minimal step from capitals to lowercase, moves along smoothly beneath.
gen-fs-azeret-mono-montserrat: Technical through and through, Azeret Mono sets its fixed-width letters in wide, spaced-out words. Montserrat below it has a thickness that never shifts with direction, and its oversized e and a openings let the line glide like wire.
gen-fs-be-vietnam-pro-fs-karma: Crisp sans up top, a settled serif below. Be Vietnam Pro is best at constant stroke width and daylight in its curves, while Karma is best at quiet, classic modulation.
gen-fs-be-vietnam-pro-roboto-slab: Clean lines up top, with a slab-serif underneath. Be Vietnam Pro traces every curve like one marker stroke, and Roboto Slab sits beside it feeling precise and structured.
gen-fs-bespoke-slab-montserrat: Montserrat opens things up with generous white space before each curve and a line that glides like wire. And Bespoke Slab, a serif with a high-set midline, brings the bookish dignity that this sans has no thick-thin modulation to offer.
gen-fs-bespoke-stencil-fs-chillax: Chillax reads loose and casual, its curves left unfinished like a pen lifted mid-loop. Bespoke Stencil stays commanding and industrial above it, so the body feels like a relaxed breath after something blunt, made for easy reading.
gen-fs-bespoke-stencil-fs-fira-sans: Bespoke Stencil stamps in with industrial command, then Fira Sans replies in tubelike lines of constant weight. The standout is Fira Sans's larger-than-usual x-height, which keeps every line legible.
gen-fs-bespoke-stencil-fs-public-sans: Commanding from the first glance, Bespoke Stencil is industrial and blunt at the top. Public Sans, a plain sans, does the quieter job below, with a hefty lowercase and broad counters that feel trustworthy.
gen-fs-bespoke-stencil-fs-ranade: Ranade reads organic and spread out, with stroke ends set far apart and weight that shifts only slightly. But Bespoke Stencil's commanding, industrial heading against that loose sans is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-fs-bespoke-stencil-montserrat: Montserrat reads wide and friendly, with room before every curve. Against Bespoke Stencil's commanding, industrial heading, its joins stay full where strokes meet, and that sturdy shared feel is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-fs-bevellier-fs-quicksand: Graceful and a bit sophisticated, Bevellier cuts its single-weight strokes tight, with a wide-looking lowercase. Quicksand, a sans, lets tall bowls like blown glass bulbs sit comfortably in small doses, and that soft contrast is the draw.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-graduate: Graduate reads dignified and bookish, with generous white between letters and capitals nearly level with the lowercase. And Bevellier crowns it with stencil-cut, single-weight lettering that sits graceful and tight.
gen-fs-bevellier-noto-serif: Bevellier brings a stencil-cut, single-weight look with a high, wide lowercase, while Noto Serif adds a modest pencil-line taper. Better for a few paragraphs than for a whole chapter.
gen-fs-bevellier-poppins: Poppins reads modern and clean, with loose curves and sturdy tall lowercase. Bevellier does its best work up top, cutting flat and graceful letters tightly together, while the sans below keeps every stroke smooth and unfussy.
gen-fs-bonny-fs-hind: Hind runs on lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals, with string-like strokes and c endings that never curl inward. Bonny brings literary refinement; Hind brings steady, workmanlike sans clarity.
gen-fs-bonny-fs-literata: Refined is the word for Bonny, a serif whose curves gape and whose strokes vary just moderately in weight. Literata brings the same bookish build, with sturdy thin lines and wide, unclosed mouths on its round letters.
gen-fs-bonny-fs-synonym: Bonny gives the heading a smooth, modest weight gradient. Synonym lays down a plain sans stripe of constant ink with generous openings, so a long passage moves along like a quiet, dependable road.
gen-fs-bonny-gf-cascadia-mono: Cascadia Mono reads compact and modern, its characters standing like pins in a wide board. Bonny earns its keep big and short, where its shifting stroke widths and gaping curves can be noticed.
gen-fs-bonny-gf-orbit: Literary Bonny sets tight lines with moderately modulated strokes and curves that gape. Orbit brings a plain sans counterpart, each character floating apart, so give it a little more size than feels necessary.
gen-fs-bonny-inter: Refined Bonny leads with a mid-range stroke contrast and gaping curves, tight-set and literary. Inter then runs smooth as a tube, its big counters keeping a full page of text open and unhurried.
gen-fs-bonny-manrope: Refined Bonny lets light modulation ripple through its strokes, with gaping curves and tight-set lines. But Manrope's bright openings and drawn-string steadiness give the pair its strongest quality: a gentle shift from literary to approachable.
gen-fs-bonny-montserrat: Approachable Montserrat glides under the eye, with oversized counters and generous white space before each curve. And Bonny earns its keep big and brief, where its mellow thick-thin shifts and literary air can show.
gen-fs-bonny-roboto-slab: Bonny sets a literary, refined tone with tight lines and gaping curves. Its subtle thick-thin modulation does the refined talking, while Roboto Slab, a slab-serif, brings a dominant middle zone and open throats.
gen-fs-boxing-fs-bespoke-sans: Boxing is energetic and bold, with a wire-bent look across each word. It earns its keep big and short, while Bespoke Sans, sharp and refined, is made for brief bursts of reading.
gen-fs-boxing-fs-roundo: Generous sidebearings and wide channels into every bowl give Boxing its bold, energetic stance. Roundo handles the quiet part, its n arch matching the stem, with unclogged counters suited to a brief stretch of text.
gen-fs-boxing-fs-synonym: Synonym reads as a clean, dependable stripe of ink in a sans with open curves. Boxing is the one to bring energy, with bold, loosely spaced letters, while Synonym is not meant for long paragraphs.
gen-fs-boxing-sora: Sora reads precise and geometric, with no swelling where a curve turns and a c and s held widely apart. Boxing brings the energy, earning its keep big and short with bold, generously spaced letters.
gen-fs-britney-cabin: Britney is a relaxed, expressive calligraphic hand with very narrow room around each letter. And Cabin, warm sans-serif tubing with open terminals, wants some extra size, since this pair is best with little text.
gen-fs-britney-fs-bespoke-sans: Britney is expressive, a calligraphic hand with tight spacing. Its best trick is a stroke that never thins, met by Bespoke Sans, a sharp sans-serif with open curve ends, made for brief reading.
gen-fs-britney-fs-literata: Relaxed Britney writes in a plain, unshaded line that never swells. Britney does the expressive work; Literata, a bookish serif with strokes that differ just enough, takes the reading, though not dense pages.
gen-fs-britney-fs-roundo: Roundo reads neutral and geometric, its n arch matching the stem and its small counters staying unclogged. Make Britney small and its tight calligraphic hand turns fussy, or enlarge the sans-serif body and it loses its comfort in small doses.
gen-fs-britney-fs-synonym: Britney writes in a relaxed, calligraphic hand with very narrow spacing. Synonym steps in below with generous curve openings to keep things readable, though neither font is made for pages of dense text.
gen-fs-britney-nunito-sans: Relaxed, that's Britney, a squeezed calligraphic script whose curves hold a thread-like line. Nunito Sans gives it a soft, open-mouthed partner, and that gentle handoff is the pair's best trick, better for brief copy.
gen-fs-chubbo-fs-gambetta: Soft marker-tip roundness, flat and friendly, runs through Chubbo without a single swelling stroke. And Gambetta moves with a gentle ebb and flow of weight, giving the pairing a bookish grace.
gen-fs-chubbo-gf-almendra: Chubbo draws every bend as if with a marker tip, casual and inviting, with a smooth path all the way around. Almendra's deep, tall lowercase gives a dignified text serif texture over many lines.
gen-fs-chubbo-gf-epunda-slab: Marker-drawn and unshaded, Chubbo glides through every bend, while Epunda Slab brings dignified, tall rounded lowercase forms. Loose and inviting above, steadier and more formal in the text below.
gen-fs-chubbo-gf-graduate: Chubbo opens with friendly, marker-drawn letters that curve smoothly and feel casual and welcoming from the first word. Graduate, a serif with generous space between letters and no stem contrast, makes a dignified, bookish read.
gen-fs-chubbo-gf-noto-sans-buginese: Chubbo moves around each bend like a marker tip, crossbars matching the stems in thickness. And Noto Sans Buginese keeps things modern, with open letter mouths and short ascenders.
gen-fs-chubbo-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Marker-tip curves, smooth all the way round, define Chubbo. Noto Sans Syriac adds tall, bulb-like lowercase bowls and wide, easy s turns in a modern sans-serif, so the two read as friendly and approachable.
gen-fs-chubbo-gf-port-lligat-slab: Round, marker-drawn, and easygoing, Chubbo leads with an inviting casual look. Port Lligat Slab, a literary serif with wide porthole counters and curves with room to breathe, is the pair's strongest card.
gen-fs-chubbo-roboto-slab: Roboto Slab reads precise and structured, its middle zone dominating each line. Chubbo's marker-traced strokes bring a casual welcome up top, so reading down the page moves from friendly to firm.
gen-fs-erode-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Erode keeps its strokes lightly modulated, with no harsh thin spots. That crispness earns its keep big and short, while Be Vietnam Pro draws pencil-like lines that never thicken or thin.
gen-fs-erode-general-sans: Erode shifts only mildly between heavy and light strokes, so its crisp letters feel like close relatives and keep a prominent x-height. General Sans then reads smoothly, its steady pen pressure carrying you along.
gen-fs-erode-gf-cascadia-code: Cascadia Code leaves wide gaps between neighbors and keeps a wire-like monoline skeleton, while Erode thins only moderately, like soft-metal type. Cascadia Code makes extended reading a plain, shade-free walk, since no calligraphic shading guides the eye.
gen-fs-erode-montserrat: Erode brings crisp, graceful strokes with a mellow swing from heavy to light. Montserrat takes over with oversized counters and bent-paperclip strokes, so the page moves from tailored detail into open, friendly space.
gen-fs-erode-roboto-slab: Roboto Slab is a structured slab-serif that lets the middle zone of each line dominate. But what stands out is the shared crispness: Erode's letterpress-slug variation meets Roboto Slab's low contrast.
gen-fs-excon-fs-familjen-grotesk: Familjen Grotesk reads lively, with bowls left open on one side and lowercase standing tall against capitals. And Excon, crowded like chalk marks on a full slate, is the denser partner with uniformly thick round letters.
gen-fs-excon-fs-fira-sans: Fira Sans reads with s curves that open wide at both ends and a larger-than-usual x-height. Excon shares that build, so a full page of Fira Sans keeps its flat, unshaded rhythm from top to bottom.
gen-fs-excon-fs-karma: Excon packs its letters tightly, like chalk marks on a full slate, with a single stroke weight throughout. Karma finishes its terminals away from the stem and tapers like a sharpened carpenter's pencil line.
gen-fs-excon-fs-ranade: Ranade sets its stroke ends far apart and its type widely spaced. Over a full page that gentle shift in weight feels organic, a softer partner for Excon, whose every stroke ends at a measured thickness.
gen-fs-excon-gf-lisu-bosa: Lisu Bosa lets its counters spill into the surrounding space. Excon, bent from a single wire, would feel cramped if made small, while Lisu Bosa keeps a mellow shift in weight.
gen-fs-excon-inter: Inter reads smooth and tube-like, its big counters opening up inside a tall lowercase. And Excon, crowded and chalky by comparison, shares that same sturdy build, which is what makes the two feel related.
gen-fs-excon-rubik: Rubik's lowercase looks big beside its capitals, soft and clear. Excon crowds its letters tight like chalk on a slate, while Rubik's open round shapes keep the text easy to follow down the page.
gen-fs-expose-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Tight and striking, Expose barely pauses between x-height and caps. Be Vietnam Pro slips in underneath with curves like bent steel rods and endings that never crowd each other.
gen-fs-expose-fs-familjen-grotesk: Compressed and striking, Expose barely stops to breathe. Familjen Grotesk loosens things up with lively bowls left open on one side and lowercase that stands tall, good when the text stays brief.
gen-fs-expose-gf-armata: Expose packs its x-height and caps almost flush, a compressed cadence that barely pauses for breath. Give Armata a little more size, since its sans-serif spacing is generous.
gen-fs-expose-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Striking in its compressed rhythm, Expose barely pauses between lowercase and capitals. And Noto Sans Lisu answers that tension with generously opened s curves, so the whole pairing feels refined without ever getting fussy.
gen-fs-expose-gf-noto-sans-old-persian: Noto Sans Old Persian breathes, its lofty lowercase full of space. Expose does its best work tightly packed, striking and refined, where this body font lets the white space in.
gen-fs-expose-gf-savate: Tight and striking, Expose squeezes its lowercase almost up to cap height. Savate is the open-jawed foil, its tall rounded o nearly matching a capital O, with sturdy hairlines and a light modulation.
gen-fs-expose-mulish: Mulish reads wire-like and friendly, with a large x-height and short ascenders. But if Expose were made small, its compressed cadence would lose its punch against that sans-serif body.
gen-fs-expose-poppins: Poppins is a plain sans whose lines keep their width through every turn, with a tall, sturdy lowercase. Against Expose's compressed, striking look, that steadiness is the strongest card.
gen-fs-expose-rubik: Tightly packed and refined, Expose hardly leaves any gap between its small letters and capitals. But Rubik's soft, large lowercase and open round shapes give the pairing its strongest quality: a crisp, friendly counterweight.
gen-fs-familjen-grotesk-fs-karma: Contemporary and unfussy, Familjen Grotesk lets white space leak into its big round bowls. Karma, a serif with terminals that stop well short of the stem, adds a trustworthy, gently modulated voice that never snags the eye.
gen-fs-gambarino-archivo: Gambarino's heavy, ink-flooded stems taper into hairline joins where the curves meet them. And Archivo, a sans-serif with a tall lowercase, opens its curves outward and keeps things approachable beneath that drama.
gen-fs-gambarino-cabin: Cabin reads warm and clean, its letters like bent tubing with terminals left easy and open. But Gambarino brings the drama with heavy stems and hairline whiskers, while Cabin's constant stroke keeps things steady.
gen-fs-gambarino-dm-sans: DM Sans reads friendly and approachable, a sans-serif whose wide-set terminals on the s keep each word easy on the eye. Gambarino's pale hairline threads between black stems supply the drama above it.
gen-fs-gambarino-fs-chillax: Gambarino hits hard, with heavy stems and hairlines that nearly vanish. Chillax then relaxes the read, a spaghetti-like line with no contrast at all, so text flows loose and casual.
gen-fs-gambarino-fs-roundo: Dramatic ink-heavy stems lead the way in Gambarino, with hairline tips. Roundo follows in geometric, even-handed lines, its horizontals as stout as its verticals, so paragraphs would move along smoothly without any flicker.
gen-fs-gambarino-fs-spline-sans: Dramatic, ink-heavy Gambarino stems carry hairline crossbars that almost vanish. Spline Sans works beneath it, every stroke the same weight and its curves left open, so the drama stays up top.
gen-fs-gambarino-gf-lexend-peta: Swollen curves tapering into hairline ends give Gambarino its drama, and Lexend Peta meets that with curves drawn like a technical pen. Its wide-mouthed c shapes make the strongest single quality here the sheer difference in stroke.
gen-fs-gambarino-montserrat: Gambarino has round letters with fat sides and hairline tops, moderate in lowercase height. And Montserrat, a sans with a high lowercase, glides along like marker-drawn wire, so the two feel like velvet against a smooth wire.
gen-fs-gambarino-poppins: Poppins keeps its curves loose and tall, with no shading at all. Gambarino is the showman, heavy black stems against razor hairlines, while Poppins just lets the words run along smoothly.
gen-fs-gambarino-work-sans: Work Sans reads with a high, tidy line and open-tipped curves. Gambarino's heavy stems and hairline strokes give the page drama, and the sans beneath them simply keeps the text moving.
gen-fs-hoover-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Hoover's e has a wide, funnel-shaped throat that you notice right away. Be Vietnam Pro follows with a uniform, bent-rod stroke, so long paragraphs move along without any fuss.
gen-fs-hoover-roboto-slab: Roboto Slab fills the middle of each line with dense, structured texture. Hoover's bookish serif sits above it, and a long passage would feel steady, with open a, c, e and s keeping the rhythm easy.
gen-fs-kalam-instrument-sans: Cozy is the first impression, thanks to Kalam's hand-drawn, tightly bundled lines. Instrument Sans brings a crisp, unvarying stroke with open pincer-like c shapes, and that gap between hand and machine is what makes the pair memorable.
gen-fs-kalam-montserrat: Inviting and homey, Kalam looks drawn by hand and packed close together. Montserrat's wire-light line and oversized, generous counters spread out beneath it, so the page feels both personal and spacious.
gen-fs-karma-fs-epilogue: Epilogue reads as curvy and loose, with a wire-thin skeleton and stubby ascender tips on tall-bodied letters. Karma's gently thickened curves above it make a longer read feel warm.
gen-fs-karma-fs-merriweather-sans: Soft, tall and rounded: Karma has modest curve stress and a visible gap through each s. Merriweather Sans looks sturdy and large, its e opening clearly to the right, so whole paragraphs move along without tiring.
gen-fs-karma-fs-public-sans: Public Sans has a hefty lowercase and broad, open counters. Karma does its best work in the mild letterpress-like shading of its curves, while Public Sans simply delivers solid, low-contrast text.
gen-fs-karma-gf-cascadia-code: Rounded and relaxed, Karma shows a see-through s and curves that thicken at the shoulders. Cascadia Code, wire-thin and widely spaced, is the opposite, and that tension between shaded serif and uniform monoline is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-fs-karma-rubik: Comfortable and refined, Karma leads with rounded tall lowercase and a restrained swell in its curves. And Rubik, a soft sans-serif with big, open lowercase, gives that polish a friendlier voice.
gen-fs-khand-fs-gambetta: Khand draws crisp, tightly spaced letters with a ballpoint's plain line weight. Where it stays flat and direct, the text serif Gambetta adds a subtle pen-like swing in its bowls and wide channels into each counter.
gen-fs-khand-newsreader: Khand packs crisp sans-serif letters tightly together, with no thick or thin strokes anywhere, including the w. Newsreader brings the quiet authority, built from restrained stroke contrast and open curves.
gen-fs-kohinoor-zerone-archivo: Kohinoor Zerone bends round letters like wire in one constant, pen-like line. Archivo adds editorial muscle beneath it, its sans-serif curves opening outward and its commanding x-height holding firm against all that wire.
gen-fs-kohinoor-zerone-fs-roundo: Small counters stay unclogged in Roundo, a geometric plain sans whose n has arch and stem matching, which suits brief copy. Yet Kohinoor Zerone is the one for display, drawing round letters like bent wire.
gen-fs-kola-archivo: Kola brings a bold, distinctive display face with moderate lowercase height and a plain build. Archivo follows with taller lowercase and outward-opening curves, and that editorial height is the strongest thing about the pair.
gen-fs-kola-fs-chillax: Kola is bold and distinctive, with plain, unfussy letterforms. Chillax follows with casual, spaghetti-like lines and pen-lifted curves left open, a relaxed plain sans that is happiest over a few lines.
gen-fs-kola-fs-literata: Bold and plain up top, scholarly below, with a clear turn between the two. Kola holds the display work with its low-contrast shapes, while Literata, a classic serif, handles the text with sturdy thin lines and wide mouths.
gen-fs-kola-fs-neco: Kola's plainness is the first thing you see, a bold display face with low contrast throughout. But Neco, a dignified classic serif with hairlines only slightly lighter than its stems, is comfortable in small doses.
gen-fs-kola-fs-ranade: Bold and distinctive, Kola sets a plain display tone at moderate lowercase height before Ranade, a plain sans with taller lowercase, takes over. Its widely spaced, organic line gives the text room.
gen-fs-kola-plus-jakarta-sans: Loud, plain and unmistakable, Kola announces itself at once. Kola is best at making a statement, while Plus Jakarta Sans, built like bent tubing, is better suited to concise text.
gen-fs-merriweather-sans-fs-karma: Cozy sums up Merriweather Sans, whose big counters let you see right into each curve. Karma, a text serif with weighty stems and terminals clear of the stem, adds a trustworthy, classic counterpoint.
gen-fs-merriweather-sans-roboto-slab: Big-hearted letters meet sturdy ones: Merriweather Sans opens its curves wide while Roboto Slab, a slab-serif, stays structured. Merriweather Sans really earns its keep when it's big and brief.
gen-fs-new-title-cabin: Tall, bold and chain-linked, New Title looks built from fine links. Cabin then eases the reading, its bent-tubing sans forms and open terminals keeping paragraph after paragraph warm and unhurried.
gen-fs-new-title-fs-erode: New Title's lowercase stands unusually tall, its letters locked together like links in a fine chain. Erode, a text serif with a gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight, lets extended reading move along with quiet dignity.
gen-fs-new-title-fs-karma: Slender turns meet robust downstrokes in the body text, which reads trustworthy and classic. Karma feels quiet, settled, and sure of itself beside New Title's loud, tall, chain-linked letters.
gen-fs-new-title-fs-pally: Pally, a sans-serif built on one fixed nib width and open c shapes, sits under New Title's tall, bold chain of letters. Extended paragraphs of it would feel relaxed, clean, and quietly unhurried.
gen-fs-new-title-fs-paquito: Paquito reads confident and approachable, with caps barely taller than its lowercase. Beneath New Title's tall, chain-linked display letters, that serif keeps things friendly, so the bold top never overwhelms.
gen-fs-new-title-fs-roundo: New Title packs tall lowercase into tight, chain-like rows. What stands out most is lowercase height, towering in New Title but moderate in Roundo, a sans-serif with unclogged counters.
gen-fs-new-title-fs-spline-sans: New Title packs its tall lowercase into tight, chain-like links that read bold and modern. Spline Sans opens up with wide gaps at its curve ends, and its matched strokes make the strongest contrast of the two.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-biorhyme: Modern and tightly linked, New Title stands tall in its lowercase, like a fine chain pulled across the line. BioRhyme, a serif with brush-lifted curve endings, would sit nicely a few sizes down.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-domine: Lowercase letters locked together like links in a fine chain give New Title its tall, modern punch. Domine, a serif, handles the quieter job, with breathing space inside each curve and a lightly engraved contrast.
gen-fs-new-title-gf-lisu-bosa: Tight chain-link letters, tall and modern: that's New Title, a heading that stands up straight and means it. Lisu Bosa reads sturdy and open, its large lowercase carrying paragraphs without strain.
gen-fs-new-title-roboto-slab: New Title locks its tall lowercase together like links in a fine chain. Roboto Slab, the slab-serif body, adds precise structure, with open throats and a middle zone that dominates each line.
gen-fs-nippo-fs-alpino: Small letters that stand nearly capital-sized, cut from wire: that is Nippo, technical through and through. Alpino is cozy and tight, better for a quick look than for paragraphs.
gen-fs-nippo-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Proud little letters cut from wire: that's Nippo. Pilcrow Rounded packs tight spacing around big counters, warm enough for a quick paragraph but made for brevity, not a marathon.
gen-fs-nippo-fs-quicksand: Quicksand is all blown-glass bulbs and open endings. Next to Nippo, with its wire-cut, near-capital letters, it feels much gentler, a soft, friendly counterweight best kept to brief text.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-atkinson-hyperlegible-ne: Wire-thin and proud, Nippo stands tall beside Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, whose washer-sized eyes and unlatched rounds feel contemporary and approachable. What stands out most is how clearly each letter speaks.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-roboto: Roboto reads clean, with generous mouths on its round letters. Nippo cuts every stem and curve from one gauge of tubing, while Roboto keeps its capitals and lowercase close in height.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-stack-sans-headline: Wiry, technical, and almost all capitals in feel. Nippo excels at sharp, cut-wire display lettering, while Stack Sans Headline keeps its monoline sans-serif forms crisp and open when the sizes get tiny.
gen-fs-nippo-montserrat: Montserrat glides under the eye, its curves entered through generous white space, while Nippo's wiry strokes cut sharp above it. Shrink the heading and its proud small letters lose that bite.
gen-fs-nippo-rubik: Rubik reads soft and clear, its big lowercase and open round letters holding up at small sizes. And Nippo's cut-wire strokes give the heading a technical edge, with small letters standing nearly capital-sized.
gen-fs-nunito-fs-karma: Soft and cozy up top: Nunito's curves refuse to close, and Karma's serif terminals finish well clear of the stem below. Karma's gentle modulation never snags the eye on its way.
gen-fs-oswald-bitter: Oswald packs its rows of text tightly, confident and strong. What stands out most is grounded footing: Bitter, a slab-serif with a very large lowercase eye and a see-through gap in each s.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-chillax: Oswald sets tight, confident rows of text in a display voice. Chillax loosens things up with a smooth, tube-like line and casual pen-lifted curves that leave their loops unfinished.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-epilogue: Oswald brings tightly knit, confident rows of display text. Epilogue, a plain sans with a tall-bodied lowercase and wire-like monoline strokes, supplies the pair's most striking quality: curvy, unclamped looseness.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-erode: Tightly knit rows give Oswald its confident, strong look. Erode, a text serif, keeps a tall middle band and shallow ascenders, and its weight ebbs and flows so reading glides on.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-gambetta: Oswald does strength best, packing tightly knit rows with confidence. Gambetta, a text serif, does bookish grace, with wide channels into each counter and soft accents of heavier strokes.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-hind: Tightly knit rows of confident display type make Oswald hard to miss. Hind, a sans with lowercase nearly matching the capitals and strokes steady as a drawn string, keeps reading smooth and unhurried.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-hoover: Tight, confident, strong: Oswald stacks its rows close and means it. Hoover, a serif with a generous entry into the e's eye and compressed ascenders, makes reading feel refined and sturdy.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-public-sans: Confident and tightly knit, Oswald packs its rows of text into a strong, compact block that holds attention. Public Sans loosens things with a hefty lowercase and broad, open counters.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-ranade: Oswald packs its rows of text tight and tall, a display face with a low-key, confident stroke variation. Ranade loosens everything up, with stroke ends far apart and a slight, rubbery shift in weight.
gen-fs-oswald-fs-spline-sans: Oswald is confident and strong, its rows of text tightly knit. Spline Sans loosens the mood with approachable, plain sans lettering whose horizontals weigh exactly as much as its verticals.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-armata: Confident, tightly knit rows make Oswald feel strong at a glance. Armata, the plain sans here, spaces its characters generously and lets lowercase fill most of the letter height.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-cardo: Tight and muscular, Oswald packs its rows close above the literary serif of Cardo. And where Oswald is best at confident display, Cardo does its best work in thins that never turn spindly.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-cascadia-code: Confident and compact, Oswald holds its lines close. Cascadia Code, a sans with a wire-like monoline skeleton and a taller lowercase, stands apart with spacing you can't miss and smooth, unobstructed curves.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-chakra-petch: Chakra Petch reads contemporary, its round letters cupped rather than clenched and its strokes held to one width. Oswald, meanwhile, packs confident, tightly knit rows into a heading, and the body font keeps things professional with its uniform line.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-domine: Tightly knit rows give Oswald a confident, strong stance up top. And while Oswald commands the display role, Domine, the text serif here, gives every curve a breathing space and a refined, dignified finish.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-epunda-slab: Oswald sets a confident, tightly knit display line over a moderate lowercase. And Epunda Slab, a serif, contrasts it with tall rounded forms and a visibly gaping c, which is the pair's most striking quality.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-kosugi-maru: Kosugi Maru glows like neon tubing, with stroke ends set far apart. Under Oswald's confident, tightly knit heading, this plain sans keeps its stroke widths put from stem to curve, so paragraphs would move along smoothly.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-line-seed-jp: Oswald stands tall and tightly knit, all confidence. LINE Seed JP answers it with strokes of uniform thickness and counters that let the eye slip right through, which is the real charm here.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-noto-sans-newa: Tight, strong, and sure of itself up top. Noto Sans Newa takes over below with a tall lowercase and a clearly open e, giving Oswald's compact rows a taller, looser partner.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-port-lligat-slab: Port Lligat Slab reads literary, with wide round counters like portholes. Shrink Oswald down and its tight, confident rows lose their punch, while the slab's hugging letters would still hold up if enlarged.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-quando: Bookish in spirit, this pairing starts with a heading that is confident and compact. Quando follows with sparse, widely spaced letters and a big middle zone, so Oswald delivers the punch and the serif delivers the room.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-savate: Oswald packs its heading into tight, strong rows with a low, restrained thick-thin ratio, set against Savate's taller, sturdier hairlines. The two differ most in height, and that gap does the work.
gen-fs-oswald-gf-sour-gummy: Tight and bold above, loose and crisp below. Sour Gummy keeps wide gaps between its letters, so a long page of it would read cleanly even at tiny sizes beside Oswald's compact lines.
gen-fs-oswald-nunito-sans: Nunito Sans keeps its small-letter curves open-mouthed and soft, sitting directly beneath the tightly knit, confident rows of Oswald. Text running in it should feel gentle, neutral and unforced.
gen-fs-oswald-outfit: Approachable describes Outfit, whose curves finish well before they close. Oswald is best at packing confident, tight rows, while Outfit does its best work with strokes bent like cable at one width.
gen-fs-oswald-sora: Oswald crowds its letters together into a strong display heading, while Sora's uppercase is built from lines of one constant thickness. A long page of Sora would feel precise.
gen-fs-oswald-space-grotesk: Space Grotesk builds each glyph from a ribbon of constant width, with counters open like a hollow reed, against Oswald's tight, strong rows. That wire-like body against a dense heading is its best quality.
gen-fs-panchang-archivo: Panchang pushes out wide, confident strokes that never pinch at a curve. Archivo sits taller in the lowercase and more editorial, so the two feel like a loud voice and a friendly one trading lines.
gen-fs-panchang-fs-fira-sans: Panchang's strokes hold steady like a drawn string, with open space between every stem and curve. Fira Sans follows with a larger lowercase and no thick-and-thin swing, giving the display face a sturdy partner.
gen-fs-panchang-fs-gambetta: Panchang glows with a thickness like neon glass tubing, bold and expressive across the top of the page. Gambetta's gently shifting strokes stay comfortable in small doses.
gen-fs-panchang-montserrat: Panchang's strokes run with the steadiness of a drawn string, never snagging on a closed-up bowl. And Montserrat glides beneath it with generous white space leading into each curve, so the heading feels confident and the body feels welcoming.
gen-fs-panchang-outfit: Outfit reads clean and approachable, its curves finishing well before they close. Its strokes are bent like cable, so the sans stays better for brief copy while Panchang carries the bolder, display-sized voice above it.
gen-fs-panchang-sora: Panchang keeps wide stretches of blank between each stem and curve, confident and expressive. Its job is display flair, while Sora, precise and geometric, is good for a handful of lines.
gen-fs-paquito-fs-asap: Lowercase forms that fill the line like capitals give Paquito a sturdy, warm presence. Asap, the plain sans below, reads easily across many lines, its open c arcs and near-capital body height keeping the rhythm steady.
gen-fs-paquito-fs-public-sans: Sturdy, warm, and nearly all capital-height in its lowercase, Paquito makes a firm opening. But Public Sans answers with a hefty lowercase and broad open counters, so the serif heading and the sans-serif body both feel dependable.
gen-fs-paquito-montserrat: Montserrat reads geometric and approachable, with white space leading into each curve and a line that glides like wire. And its monoline strokes set against Paquito's sturdy serif give the pair a clear, memorable contrast.
gen-fs-pencerio-fs-chillax: Graceful and formal, Pencerio writes in a calligraphic hand with closely fitted word shapes. Chillax loosens everything up beneath it, its same-width strokes trailing like spaghetti and made for short stretches of reading.
gen-fs-pencerio-outfit: A calligraphic hand with tightly clenched word shapes gives Pencerio its formal grace, and it is comfortable in small doses. But Outfit counters with plain sans lines bent like cable, unvarying in thickness and finishing their curves before they close.
gen-fs-pilcrow-rounded-fs-erode: Erode reads dignified, with a tall middle band and soft shifts in stroke weight. Pilcrow Rounded sits above it in smooth, plain outlines, so the headings feel friendly while the text stays gently shaded.
gen-fs-pilcrow-rounded-fs-karma: Pilcrow Rounded sets friendly, tightly packed letters with a lowercase as dense as poured lead type. Karma comes in behind as a trustworthy text serif, its terminals finishing clear of the stem and its strokes thinning gently.
gen-fs-pramukh-rounded-archivo: Pramukh Rounded packs its glyphs close, with bowls tipped open like a ladle, and it looks best big and brief. Archivo follows in the same spirit, a sans with curves that open outward and a commanding x-height.
gen-fs-pramukh-rounded-fs-familjen-grote: Pramukh Rounded bunches its glyphs tight, with barely a gap between them. Familjen Grotesk, the plain sans beside it, shares that build, so the two feel like one friendly, lively voice.
gen-fs-pramukh-rounded-fs-hind: Hind keeps its lowercase close to the capitals' height. Its curves match the stems exactly, which sets off the tightly bunched, ladle-bowled Pramukh Rounded and makes the shared friendliness the strongest thing here.
gen-fs-pramukh-rounded-fs-hoover: Pramukh Rounded packs its glyphs tight, with open bowls tipped toward you like a ladle. Hoover, the text serif underneath, brings compressed ascenders and a generous e eye, so paragraphs feel refined and robust.
gen-fs-pramukh-rounded-gf-graduate: Friendly describes Pramukh Rounded, with glyphs bunched tight together. Graduate, the serif, spaces letters generously and draws stems and joins with no contrast, so thin strokes never vanish in glare.
gen-fs-public-sans-fs-erode: Public Sans brings broad terminal gaps and a high x-height. Erode, a text serif, adds a lightly swelling stroke in each rounded letter, so the headings feel modern while the body reads editorial.
gen-fs-quicksand-gf-graduate: Short capitals among tall small letters mark Quicksand, whose tube-like stroke keeps a bright opening at every curve. Graduate, a serif, handles the dignified, bookish work with generous spacing and no contrast between stems and joins.
gen-fs-quilon-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Tight, warm, quietly rounded: Pilcrow Rounded packs its tall lowercase close, with curves that never quite shut. Quilon is the one that flexes, swelling gently in its stroke; Pilcrow stays level.
gen-fs-quilon-fs-ranade: Quilon swells and thins in a slow, editorial rhythm. Ranade, spaced wide and shifting only slightly in weight, gives the pair its strongest quality: a headline with presence over text that breathes.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-lisu-bosa: Lisu Bosa is a text serif with tall, sturdy lowercase and counters that spill generously into the space around them. And Quilon above it keeps the editorial tone going with its own gentle swell of stroke.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-savate: Editorial and commanding, Quilon swells and thins calmly across large open counters, while Savate lays down sturdy hairlines and open jaws. That plain sans keeps text feeling clean and contemporary throughout.
gen-fs-quilon-instrument-sans: Commanding and editorial, Quilon varies its stroke with a measured thick-thin ratio, while Instrument Sans looks cut from strips of equal width. Paragraphs in the plain sans come across clean and modern.
gen-fs-rajdhani-gf-bhutuka-expanded-one: BhuTuka Expanded One slows the eye to a leisurely walk, all curvy and authoritative. Rajdhani's dense, tightly woven strips make a brisker contrast, so a slightly larger body size would suit it.
gen-fs-rajdhani-newsreader: Authoritative is the mood Newsreader gives the body, while Rajdhani above it stays clean and modern with tightly woven lines. Newsreader then carries a long page as a text serif with restrained stress and open jaws on its curves.
gen-fs-rajdhani-source-serif-4: Dignified and a touch stern, Source Serif 4 tightens its strokes slightly at the tops of curves and leaves a gaping c. And Rajdhani's marker-tip letters sit above it, modern where the serif is letterpress-minded.
gen-fs-ranade-fs-karma: Ranade leads with friendly, widely tracked lowercase that looks bigger than its capitals. Karma, a text serif with a very small gap between x-height and cap height, can go up a size to hold its own.
gen-fs-ranade-gf-graduate: Graduate reads dignified and bookish, with generous white between letters and an unshaded, steady outline. But Ranade is the friendlier one, its mild taper like wire rolled barely flat, while Graduate does its best work holding a line.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-archivo: Bold marker lines up top, a commanding body below. Red Hat Display does best at confident, constant-width lines with daylight in every curve, while Archivo does best at outward-opening curves and a commanding x-height.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-clash-grotesk: Contemporary and bold, Red Hat Display draws with a marker's constant width. Clash Grotesk, a sans-serif, drops stroke modulation entirely, so its clean, approachable lines sit beside the heading's visible daylight without competing.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-fs-alpino: Alpino reads cozy and a bit squat, its tall body making ascenders look short. Red Hat Display handles the smooth, plotter-like heading work, and Alpino keeps the casual text feeling snug with curve endings held well apart.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-fs-karma: Red Hat Display moves with a skimming ease, its stroke never changing weight. Karma's text serif then settles in with a mild, letterpress-like modulation and terminals clear of the stem, so a long passage feels trustworthy.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-fs-literata: Red Hat Display keeps one line width through every curve and straight, like a marker on paper. Literata serif is the bookish counterpart, with thin strokes only slightly slimmer than its stems.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-fs-merriweather-s: Merriweather Sans makes words look sturdy and large, with an e that opens clearly rightward. And paragraphs settle into a sturdy, unhurried rhythm under the marker-like lines of Red Hat Display.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-fs-roundo: Roundo reads geometric and tidy, its n built with arch and stem matching. Red Hat Display is the bolder voice, with a marker-like line and open curves, while the sans-serif body keeps every small counter unclogged.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-carme: Carme reads modern and open, its counters leading outward. Beneath the bold marker lines of Red Hat Display, whole paragraphs of its spaghetti-like line travel smoothly across the page.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-domine: Red Hat Display bends each letter like a single wire. It earns its keep big and brief, while Domine serif adds dignity with tall lowercase and a tempered contrast.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-faculty-glyphi: Faculty Glyphic reads low and soft, a plain sans with rounded openings. Red Hat Display draws wire-cut strokes that hold up in big sizes, while the body font is happiest in running text.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-judson: Contemporary and bold, Red Hat Display draws one marker-like line with daylight in every curve. Judson, dignified and bookish, brings brush-lifted curve ends and fine hairlines, so extended reading feels settled and deliberate.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-snippet: Red Hat Display draws everything with a marker's constant width, leaving visible daylight inside every curve. But Snippet's wire-bent words and crescent-wrench c add a quirky, approachable streak beneath the bold heading.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-instrument-sans: Red Hat Display holds one marker-like width throughout, with visible daylight inside every curve. And Instrument Sans, with its pincer-open c and unvarying stroke, gives paragraphs a clean, modern, steady pace.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-montserrat: Red Hat Display draws a marker-steady line with daylight inside every curve. Montserrat brings the real surprise: generous white space, oversized counters and a wire-smooth glide that make the pairing feel inviting.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-newsreader: Contemporary and bold, Red Hat Display draws every stroke like a marker line, with daylight inside each curve. Newsreader, a serif, keeps its stems and hairlines close, so paragraphs flow smoothly.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-nunito-sans: Bold, hairline-free letters up top, soft open-mouthed curves below: Red Hat Display sits over a low, gentle Nunito Sans. Give the heading a generous size and let the sans-serif text stay modest.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-outfit: Red Hat Display draws a marker-like line, contemporary and bold, with visible daylight inside every curve. Outfit follows with curves that finish before they close, cable-bent and unswelling, and that is the strongest quality of this sans-serif pair.
gen-fs-rosaline-nunito-sans: Nunito Sans sets soft, open-mouthed curves in small letters, quiet and neutral. And Rosaline, a flowing pen-written script with closed, sharp-edged forms, gives a handful of lines a luxurious lift above that sans-serif.
gen-fs-rx-100-fs-paquito: Paquito reads low and confident, a serif with hardly any gap between lowercase and caps. RX100 crowds its twine-like strokes into a futuristic, compact run, while Paquito is the one for a handful of lines of text.
gen-fs-segment-fs-alpino: Segment spaces its letters wide and stands tall in the middle, with counters that breathe. Alpino, a cozy sans, sits tight and compact beneath it, so the heading looks grand and the text looks handy.
gen-fs-segment-montserrat: Segment leaves wide gaps between its letters and stacks a stocky, tall middle band into every line, which feels commanding. Montserrat glides smoothly beneath it, a good fit for brief reading.
gen-fs-sharpie-fs-chillax: Expressive and bold, Sharpie crowds its letters behind what feels like a narrow slot. Chillax loosens things with open, relaxed curves that never thin at the turns, and it is made for short stretches of reading.
gen-fs-sharpie-fs-public-sans: Public Sans has a hefty lowercase and broad open counters that feel trustworthy at a glance. Over a longer stretch it would read steadily, while Sharpie keeps its tight, hairline-gapped letters up top.
gen-fs-sharpie-fs-rowan: Sharpie packs bold, expressive letters behind a hairline-thin gap, while Rowan's friendly text serif keeps every curve open. Save Sharpie for big, brief headings, and let Rowan stay in light doses.
gen-fs-spline-sans-fs-literata: Rounded, nib-like strokes with no swelling at their ends give Spline Sans an approachable, geometric look. And Literata, a bookish text serif with sturdy hairlines and wide-mouthed curves, would carry a longer stretch of reading with a quiet, sophisticated pull.
gen-fs-stardom-fs-asap: Dramatic lowercase in outsized proportions, Stardom sets thick diagonals against hairline counter-strokes for a showy look. And Asap, readable with open-arc c forms, carries a brief stretch of text without fuss.
gen-fs-styro-fs-alpino: Alpino has open, casual curves with endings kept well apart. Styro, by contrast, presses its letters together into a crowded, retro block, so it is better for brief copy than for pages of text.
gen-fs-styro-fs-bespoke-sans: Bespoke Sans reads sharp and refined, with generous space around each curve. Styro delivers crowded, retro punch from a sizable lowercase, while Bespoke Sans handles the finer, more open lines.
gen-fs-styro-fs-bespoke-slab: Bespoke Slab is a grounded, refined serif with tall bodies in every lowercase letter, not meant for long paragraphs. Bespoke Slab gets modest sizing, and Styro supplies the retro, commanding heading above it.
gen-fs-styro-fs-hoover: Retro and crowded, with letters pressed shoulder to shoulder. Styro's tight, closed shapes get relief from Hoover, a serif whose open e eyes and short ascenders keep brief text refined.
gen-fs-styro-fs-nunito: Nunito reads soft and friendly, with big round bowls and stroke ends that finish away from the stem. And the tension is the draw: Styro's closed, crowded letters against Nunito's open ones, though neither suits long paragraphs.
gen-fs-styro-fs-quicksand: Styro presses its lowercase so tight that the counters nearly shut, a retro, commanding look. Quicksand, a sans of tubular strokes and tall glassy bowls, opens everything Styro closes, which is best for quick lines.
gen-fs-styro-fs-ranade: Styro is retro and commanding, crowding its large lowercase until the counters barely open. And Ranade, a sans with widely spaced letters and a faint watercolor shift in weight, does the breathing Styro cannot.
gen-fs-styro-fs-technor: Technor reads like neon tube, cool and geometric, with one steady line thickness and a wide channel into every bowl. Styro's crowded retro punch is the hook, and best taken in sips.
gen-fs-styro-general-sans: Styro packs its big lowercase so tightly the eyes of its letters almost close, loud and retro. General Sans handles the quiet work, drawing smooth open bends at a steady pressure while Styro takes the commanding lines.
gen-fs-styro-gf-mochiy-pop-one: Mochiy Pop One reads big and round, with a very large lowercase eye and letters hung out like clothespins on a line. Styro's crowded, closed letters make the sharpest difference of all.
gen-fs-styro-gf-prompt: Styro brings retro command, its lowercase large and its letters pressed together until the openings nearly vanish. But Prompt, with oversized small letters and open apertures, feels like a window thrown wide beside it.
gen-fs-styro-instrument-sans: Retro and commanding, Styro crowds its letters until the counters almost close up. Instrument Sans would carry paragraph after paragraph smoothly, its c ends pointing apart like pincers and its strokes never varying.
gen-fs-supreme-fs-erode: Erode brings editorial dignity with a gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight. What stands out most is Supreme's tall, understated sans-serif lowercase, which gives each curve room against Erode's serif texture.
gen-fs-synonym-fs-literata: Synonym draws its small curves wide open, with joins as slim as a pipe cleaner and no flaring at the stroke ends. Literata, a classic serif, is bookish by comparison, its thin and thick lines only gently different.
gen-fs-tanker-fs-karma: Tanker turns every open curve inward, packing heavy letters with barely any gaps between them. And Karma, a serif, lets its terminals finish clear of the stem, so it carries the quieter reading while Tanker keeps to brief copy.
gen-fs-tanker-gf-graduate: Tanker hits heavy and commanding, its curves turning inward and its letters packed tight, while Graduate gives dignified, bookish letters room. Paragraphs in Graduate would move slowly and steadily, every stem alike.
gen-fs-tanker-montserrat: Heavy and commanding, Tanker packs its big lowercase tight. Montserrat has oversized e and a counters and a wire-like glide, so it handles a handful of lines while Tanker leads.
gen-fs-teko-fs-bespoke-sans: Tightly packed letters cut from strokes like bent steel rod. What stands out most is how Teko's rigid, uniform line meets the sharper, more open curves of Bespoke Sans.
gen-fs-teko-fs-karma: Teko sets tightly packed letters in strokes like bent steel rod, with no hairlines and no shadows anywhere. Karma, a classic serif, handles the quieter work with moderate contrast.
gen-fs-teko-gf-graduate: Confident from the first glance, Teko packs its steel-rod strokes together with almost no gaps, while Graduate, a serif, spaces its letters out generously. Bold meets bookish here, tight against loose, and neither backs down.
gen-fs-telma-fs-alpino: Alpino is cozy and casual, a tall-bodied sans with curve endings kept apart, though lengthy paragraphs aren't its job. Telma's graceful, pen-written script is happiest when big and brief.
gen-fs-telma-fs-familjen-grotesk: Telma flows in a graceful, understated script with a high mean line. The standout is how Telma's gradual stroke swells meet Familjen Grotesk's lively, open-sided bowls, in text made for brief reading.
gen-fs-telma-fs-hoover: Hoover is a sturdy text serif with compressed ascenders. With Telma writing the headline in flowing script, this body keeps the reading smooth, best when the text stays brief.
gen-fs-telma-fs-karma: Karma reads trustworthy and classic, its terminals finishing well away from the stem and its modulation never snagging the eye. Pen-written Telma gives it a graceful partner, best for brief text.
gen-fs-telma-fs-paquito: Paquito is a confident, approachable text serif with capitals barely taller than its lowercase, placed under Telma. Text flows comfortably across the page, though a few lines suit it best.
gen-fs-telma-montserrat: Telma writes graceful pen-made letters with a high mean line and a wide-mouthed a. And Montserrat glides beneath it, its oversized counters keeping the text pleasant in modest amounts.

gen-luckiest-guy-gf-kiwi-maru: Poured, single-width ink under a mean, high line. Luckiest Guy is built to shout, while Kiwi Maru, with generous letterspace and terminals far from the stem, is built to unfold slowly.

gen-modak-montserrat: Puffy, bouncy lettering with enormous lowercase eyes, Modak leaves every curve far from closing up. Montserrat, the sans-serif body, gives each curve plenty of white space around it.

gen-mystery-quest-gf-port-lligat-slab: Storybook letters with open-jawed curves and compact ascenders, courtesy of Mystery Quest. Port Lligat Slab brings lowercase counters like wide glass portholes, which is the pair's single best quality.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-savate: Savate reads crisp and contemporary, with a rounded o nearly matching its capital. Beneath the bookish Mystery Quest heading, that sans-serif body moves along smoothly, its hairlines sturdy enough for line after line.
gen-nixie-one-dm-sans: The body text feels friendly and open, with the terminals on its s spread well apart. DM Sans can afford a slightly larger size beneath the nostalgic, constant-stroke Nixie One heading.

gen-nixie-one-zilla-slab: Nostalgic and retro-tech, Nixie One draws a steady line with no pressure variation from top to baseline. Zilla Slab, a sturdy, technical slab-serif, gives it a firm footing underneath.
gen-orbitron-fs-hind: Hind reads with lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals, steady as a drawn string. Orbitron stretches its letters wide and shows off big open e shapes, while Hind keeps the text plain and sans-simple to follow.

gen-patua-one-fs-erode: Erode brings a tall middle band, shallow ascenders and a gentle ebb and flow of weight, under a warm heading. Erode and Patua One share an easy approachability, moderate against low contrast.
gen-permanent-marker-archivo: Loud, scrawled and grungy, Permanent Marker keeps its curves nearly shut, while Archivo opens its curves outward beneath it. Archivo's commanding x-height holds up over a longer stretch.

gen-press-start-2p-gf-cossette-titre: Retro pixel blocks sit over snug, low-profile text, each letter nestled close to the next. Press Start 2P is at its best big and brief, and Cossette Titre follows.

gen-roboto-slab-fs-merriweather-sans: Roboto Slab gives headings a structured, sturdy look, its tall lowercase making words feel large and solid. And Merriweather Sans carries that height into the text, with an open-eyed e that keeps a long page comfortable to follow.
gen-roboto-slab-fs-ranade: Ranade reads relaxed and organic, its weight shifting only slightly and its stroke ends set well apart. Roboto Slab is best at sturdy, tall-lowercase headings, whereas the plain sans below does its best work in a spread-out, gently lighter line.

gen-special-elite-fs-hoover: Hoover reads refined yet robust, its e opening generously and its ascenders cut short beneath distressed Special Elite. A page of it would feel steady, sturdy and never fussy at all.

gen-titan-one-fs-asap: Titan One is bold and playful, built from tube-like, constant-weight strokes. Asap works nicely at a modest size under big headings, its open c arcs and near-capital body height staying easy to follow.

gen-tourney-gf-open-sans: Tourney glows like neon glass, bold and athletic. Open Sans gives it a smooth, contemporary body with bulky lowercase proportions, so give the heading plenty of space to stretch out.

gen-unifrakturmaguntia-fs-public-sans: Gothic and tightly clustered, UnifrakturMaguntia towers over every word. Public Sans, a sans-serif with hefty lowercase and broad open counters, keeps text that runs for pages feeling steady and trustworthy.
gen-vast-shadow-bitter: Every stroke in Vast Shadow is cut to one width, with no thin hairlines anywhere. Bitter, a slab-serif with big lowercase eyes and see-through s shapes, grounds that vintage flash so the two sit comfortably on the page.
gen-vast-shadow-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Be Vietnam Pro reads clean, its strokes like bent steel rod and its curve endings keeping their distance. Vast Shadow, with its vintage, tall-ceilinged letters, probably wants the larger size while this sans-serif stays modest below.
gen-vast-shadow-fs-familjen-grotesk: Vintage and showy, Vast Shadow has no hairlines, only uniform stems. Familjen Grotesk, a lively sans whose lowercase stands tall and whose bowls stay unfinished on one side, loosens up the heading's solid stems.

gen-vast-shadow-fs-supreme: Supreme reads crisp, forming a heavy-looking band of text with letters held open rather than curled shut. Vast Shadow's thin, tube-like strokes give it a vintage lift, so a larger heading size would let each one show.
gen-vast-shadow-gf-savate: Eye-catching and vintage, Vast Shadow cuts every stroke to one width with round letters as heavy as straight ones. Savate, a sans with sturdy hairlines and open curves, adds light contrast beneath.
gen-vast-shadow-mulish: Vast Shadow cuts every stroke to a single width and leaves generous space around each letter, a vintage, eye-catching look. Mulish then reads smoothly paragraph after paragraph, its open curves never snagging.
gen-vast-shadow-roboto-slab: Roboto Slab reads in a precise, structured way, its slab-serif middle zone dominating the line. And down the page, Vast Shadow's rope-like vintage strokes above make that steady texture feel all the more grounded.
gen-work-sans-fs-erode: Bent tubing meets editorial dignity, with Work Sans holding a single gauge through every curve. Work Sans is best at crisp open curves, but Erode is best at a gentle ebb and flow of weight.
gen-yeseva-one-fs-chillax: Fat round bowls attach to the stem by hairline joins in Yeseva One, vintage and bookish. Chillax draws a spaghetti-like line, smooth as pen-plotter ink and relaxed enough to keep reading.
gen-yeseva-one-fs-literata: Literata reads like a sophisticated serif, its thin lines sturdy and its thicker ones only slightly heavier, with wide-open curves. Under Yeseva One's snagging fat stems, that text flows gently.
gen-yeseva-one-fs-public-sans: Trustworthy and hefty, Public Sans lays down a solid sans body with broad, open counters beneath Yeseva One's fat bowls. Swollen stems and needle-thin joins up top, sturdy low-contrast strokes below.
gen-yeseva-one-fs-roundo: Fat round bowls on hairline joins make Yeseva One the dramatic, vintage half of the pair. And Roundo, cut like a fixed-width router bit, does the quieter work of keeping small counters unclogged.
gen-yeseva-one-fs-synonym: Yeseva One gives each letter a heavy trunk and whisper-thin branches. Synonym, a sans-serif drawn with technical-pen steadiness, lays a constant-ink stripe beneath, its generous curve openings keeping that bookish drama in check.
gen-yeseva-one-sora: Sora moves with a blunt round-tip marker feel, its c and s staying widely parted at every turn. That blunt marker against Yeseva One's rope-thick stems is the real draw.
gen-young-serif-fs-bespoke-sans: Young Serif looks plain and friendly, refined without any fuss. Bespoke Sans leaves generous space between curve ends and the stem, and that sharp, refined body is what makes the pairing work.
gen-young-serif-fs-roundo: Roundo reads neutral and geometric, every small counter left unclogged. Young Serif brings the refined, friendly serif shapes above, while Roundo's sans runs as a plain stripe of constant ink beneath.
gen-yuji-mai-fs-rowan: Tight-lipped and measured, Yuji Mai spaces each word out with openings so slight the letters feel nearly sealed. And Rowan opens every curve wide, literary and friendly, a face to sip rather than gulp.
gen-zen-dots-clash-grotesk: The body text reads clean and approachable, as if drawn with a fixed-width nib. Clash Grotesk carries the running text, while Zen Dots, with lots of room around each letter, owns the tech-flavored attention up top.
gen-zen-dots-fs-alpino: Zen Dots gives every letter lots of room, a tech-flavored but friendly display voice. But Alpino, cozy and casual, stands much taller in the lowercase, with curve endings kept well apart.
gen-zen-dots-fs-asap: Zen Dots is tech-flavored and friendly, with room around each letter. Asap, a sans-serif whose c forms read as open arcs and whose body height nearly matches the capitals, gives the heading a readable partner.
gen-zen-dots-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Lots of room surrounds every Zen Dots letter, whatever the weight. Be Vietnam Pro, strokes like bent steel rod and a high mean line, keeps pages of text moving smoothly, curve endings never touching.
gen-zen-dots-gf-faculty-glyphic: Faculty Glyphic is a modern, professional sans-serif with clear openings in its rounded letters. And Zen Dots supplies the display character, tech-flavored and friendly, with lots of room around each letter.
gen-zen-dots-plus-jakarta-sans: Plus Jakarta Sans is a modern, precise sans built from monoline strokes, curve endings kept well apart. Zen Dots above, tech-flavored and friendly, loosens things up with lots of room around each letter.
gen-zen-dots-sora: Zen Dots leaves lots of room around every letter, with openings that stay generous at every weight. Sora takes over with precise, geometric strokes like neon glass, no swell at the corners.
gen-zodiak-cabin: Zodiak's strokes swing hard from heavy to hairline. Cabin sits beneath it like bent tubing, a warm sans with open endings that carry you down a long page without any fuss.
gen-zodiak-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Dramatic strokes up top, a tall lowercase below. Zodiak is at its best when thick stems meet hairlines, while Be Vietnam Pro does its best work with smooth, rod-like curves that stay well apart.
gen-zodiak-fs-public-sans: Public Sans sets a hefty lowercase with broad, open counters, solid and straightforward. And Zodiak excels at dramatic stem-and-hairline swings, whereas Public Sans thrives on trustworthy, plainly drawn text.
gen-zodiak-fs-quicksand: Heavy strokes and hairlines share every Zodiak letter, which gives it an authoritative air. And Quicksand, a plain sans with bulb-round bowls and uniform bars, makes that drama feel friendly instead of stern.
gen-zodiak-fs-ranade: Zodiak brings dignified authority, its strokes swinging hard from fat to hairline. Ranade moves in with weight that shifts only slightly and stroke ends set far apart, giving each line an organic, spread-out feel.
gen-zodiak-fs-synonym: Zodiak sets bold stems against hairline counterparts, whereas Synonym keeps stencil-cut letters at a constant width with generous curve openings. That clash of dramatic modulation and dependable plainness is the draw.
gen-zodiak-gf-lexend-giga: Zodiak arrives stately, its strokes swinging hard from heavy to fine. Lexend Giga, a sans with flat linework and wide tracking, lets each word open up, so extended text moves at a slow, measured pace.
gen-zodiak-gf-lexend-tera: Zodiak packs heavy stems and thread-thin hairlines into each letter, while Lexend Tera plots every stroke to a single measured width. Text feels spaced out, a stepping-stone stroll across the page.
gen-zodiak-gf-lexend-zetta: Heavy stems framed by hairline strokes give Zodiak its dignified, authoritative bite. And Lexend Zetta runs wide and tall-bodied in a sans-serif of constant width, so a long page moves along smoothly, unhurried and open.
gen-zodiak-gf-orbit: Sharp edges, weighty stems, razor-thin arcs: that is Zodiak. Orbit, a sans-serif with curves that stop short and letters floating apart, gives the heading a rope-like, pulse-free partner to push against.
gen-zodiak-inter: Inter reads smooth and tube-like, with big counters. Zodiak does bold stems and razor-thin horizontals best, while Inter's horizontals match its verticals, which keeps text steady and easy to follow.
gen-zodiak-mulish: Thick downstrokes sit beside hairline crossbars in Zodiak, a serif with real authority. Mulish follows in a plain sans with large, modern shapes and uniform strokes, so a long page feels friendly and unfussy.
gen-zodiak-sora: Sora is precise and geometric, with a constant stroke. Its plain sans lines have no pressure swell at the curves, which gives Zodiak's swelling, hairline-tapering stems a sharp, dignified foil.
gen-zodiak-work-sans: Work Sans draws a plain unmodulated outline with c tips held well apart, while Zodiak pairs fat stems with razor-thin hairlines. Long text moves along in a modern, unfussy way.
ibm-plex-serif-ibm-plex-sans: IBM Plex Serif has a literary, authoritative voice, with gentle weight shifts along each curve (fine for, say, a birthday invitation). IBM Plex Sans takes over as a technical, approachable sans-serif with a wide channel into every bowl.
jetbrains-mono-inter: Developer-minded and contemporary, JetBrains Mono sets fixed-width, loosely strung characters whose terminals stay open like scissor blades. Inter then carries the text as a smooth sans-serif, its big counters and tall lowercase making a long stretch glide by.
josefin-cabin: Precise, wire-cut letters from Josefin Sans sit low, while Cabin's bent-tubing curves feel warmer, say, in an empty state illustration. Low lowercase up top, a taller, friendlier body below.
libre-baskerville-manrope: Wide, loose and dignified, with authority to spare. Libre Baskerville spaces its letters generously, and Manrope's bright curve openings and steady pen line give a sans-serif that stays approachable.
lora-nunito-sans: Nunito Sans has soft, open-mouthed curves in its small letters. Lora takes the heading as a serif with authority, its thin strokes only slightly lighter than the thick ones, wide-mouthed on round forms.
merriweather-poppins: Dignified serif sturdiness up top, with rope-loose sans curves underneath it. Merriweather does best with mid-level stroke contrast and sturdy bowls, while Poppins does best at uniform, strip-cut lines with a tall body.
montserrat-merriweather: Montserrat draws a thread of ink with no swelling, stays crisp when shrunk, and stands in a tall central band. Merriweather does cozy best, with a stocky line and soft modulation.
playfair-inter: Dignified from the first glance, Playfair Display pits hairlines against fat strokes. It earns its keep big and short, while Inter keeps smooth, tube-like lines and big counters out of the way.
quilon-switzer: Editorial swagger from Quilon, in a gentle ebb and flow of stroke. Switzer's tubular, unshaded lines then carry the text, so pages of it read smoothly, friendly and never swelling.
raleway-source-serif: Source Serif 4 reads dignified, with a gaping c and bowls that thin gently at the curve tops. Raleway's wire-like line glides above it, so the serif body feels anchored beneath a lighter, precise heading.
sentient-satoshi: Tight, crisp serif forms up top, open sans letters below. Sentient's round shapes hold light back, and Satoshi lets it in through open curves, so the two trade tightness for openness.
space-grotesk-inter: Clean, geometric Space Grotesk traces its lines like one marker tip, with s terminals kept clear. And Inter, tall in the lowercase with breathing counters, feels smoother and a step taller beside it.
special-elite-dm-sans: DM Sans reads friendly and approachable, its wide-set s terminals keeping things easy going. And Special Elite pushes back with a distressed, tall x-height that fills the line, the sort of look a dj name logo might borrow.
syne-general-sans: Syne's x-height climbs almost to cap height, drawn as a plain stripe of constant ink with no pinched curves. General Sans keeps a steady pen pressure and the same tall, line-filling x-height, so the sans-serif body follows smoothly behind.
young-serif-inter: Inter reads like a smooth tube, its big counters hollow and open. Young Serif brings a friendly, refined serif voice with low contrast, and beside Inter's rope-like uniformity it feels warmer and more lived in.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-actor: Actor reads modern and tidy, with wide s curves barely curling in. Bellota's strokes all share one stylus width and its s ends hang far from the spine, which is where the pull comes from.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-graduate: Hanging s ends and stylus-width strokes mark Bellota out right away. Graduate, a serif with generous spacing and no contrast between stems and joins, brings a bookish, dignified steadiness underneath.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-noto-znamenny-musical-: Distinctive at first glance, Bellota traces every stroke at stylus width, no brush swell. Noto Znamenny Musical Notation, a sans-serif, does the clean, modern part, its terminals stopping far from the stem.
gen-gf-bellota-plus-jakarta-sans: Distinctive up top, Bellota hangs its s ends far from the spine and traces every stroke at stylus width. Plus Jakarta Sans runs on precisely, monoline with curve endings held well apart.
gen-gf-bellota-sora: Sora reads precise and geometric, its curves turning corners with no pressure swell and its c and s held widely apart. Paragraphs move along crisply, with Bellota's hanging s ends flavoring the top.
gen-gf-bellota-text-fs-familjen-grotesk: Open shapes, no shading: Bellota Text stays smooth and plain while Familjen Grotesk leaves its bowls unfinished on one side. Familjen's taller lowercase moves with a livelier stride than the heading's moderate one.
gen-gf-bellota-text-fs-ranade: Ranade reads organic and composed, its weight shifting only slightly like stretched rubber cord, stroke ends set far apart. Bellota Text, by contrast, keeps horizontals matching verticals in thickness.
gen-gf-bellota-text-fs-roundo: Bellota Text opens its curves wide and skips calligraphic shading entirely. Roundo, a sans whose n has arch and stem matching, keeps small counters unclogged under that shading-free heading.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-actor: Wire-cut strokes and open curves give Bellota Text a sharp look. Bellota Text does the attention-grabbing; Actor, a sans with wide s curves barely curled in, does the modern, clean reading.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-brawler: Bellota Text matches its diagonals to its stems and leaves its curves open, free of any calligraphic shading. Brawler's softly varied strokes add a literary, refined warmth to the text.
